notes: The frozen provider/model/hotword task surface is preserved under Vinpst. provider and model list retain ls plus -a,--available; provider install and model install retain the frozen add parser alias while presenting the clearer install name; provider/model remove retain rm; provider script edit and hotword edit retain e; model info, provider use, model use, and hotword get/set/clear remain available. Vinpst adds create/configure, installed selectors, dry-run/JSON, registry diagnostics, and safer explicit write targets without removing the frozen user tasks.

Fixed a rewrite usability regression in model use. --in-place no longer requires an explicit --config path: when omitted it reads the canonical XDG user config if present, otherwise starts from the bundled validated default, and writes the canonical user config. Existing canonical configs still receive an adjacent backup; first-time creation does not attempt to back up a nonexistent file. This makes the documented model-selection workflow executable again.

Restored the frozen save-and-reload behavior for runtime-affecting ASR mutations without reintroducing accidental D-Bus activation. Canonical provider install/create/configure/remove/use, model use, and hotword set/clear first persist validated config, then probe org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner. If org.fcitx.Vinpst is already owned they request ReloadAsrBackend; if it is stopped they leave it stopped. Bus/reload failures are warnings after a successful save rather than rollbacks, matching frozen SaveAsrConfigAndReload. --output and non-canonical config targets intentionally remain offline and never refresh the live daemon.

The explicit model-use --reload-daemon option remains as an additive Vinpst control, but ordinary canonical writes no longer require it. User docs and init/diagnostic next steps now show model use <id> --in-place and explain that an already-running daemon is refreshed automatically. Provider script edit and hotword file edit do not reload merely because an editor was opened, matching frozen behavior.

Model removal intentionally keeps a stronger Vinpst safety boundary. Frozen removes an active model, clears the preferred-model setting, saves, and reloads. Current removal refuses any model path still referenced by a local ASR provider, requiring the user to select or clear a replacement before destructive deletion; therefore the only removable models are inactive and no runtime reload is needed. This prevents a model delete from silently mutating the active ASR configuration.

Deterministic evidence includes the model/provider/hotword integration suites, strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy, and a private-session-bus smoke. The live half starts a configured daemon with two command providers and proves provider use --in-place changes the effective backend from cmd-a to cmd-b with reloaded_daemon=true. The stopped-daemon half installs a deliberately observable D-Bus activation service and proves the same canonical config mutation succeeds with reloaded_daemon=false without ever creating the activation marker, pinning the no-activation owner probe contract.

audits.title: CLI capture-device discovery and selection
notes: The frozen device task surface is preserved: device list retains the ls alias and device use accepts default or a concrete PipeWire source name. The frozen help calls the positional value an id, but the implementation actually compares and persists DeviceInfo.name rather than the numeric registry id; current target terminology is therefore more accurate while preserving the same selectable value.

Current device list intentionally keeps stronger diagnostics than frozen. Frozen collapses an empty PipeWire result and PipeWire-unavailable state into one informational message and omits even the synthetic default row. Vinpst always exposes the default target, keeps discovery order for live sources, and reports live/enumeration_error separately in JSON so a genuine empty source set can be distinguished from discovery failure. This builds on the separately audited PipeWire-device contract rather than changing backend enumeration semantics.

Restored the frozen best-effort validation behavior for non-default selections. Vinpst now checks live discovery when the PipeWire backend is available: a missing source produces a warning but is still accepted, while a discovery failure reports that the target could not be verified and likewise does not block dry-run or persistence. Builds without the PipeWire discovery feature do not invent a failure warning.

Restored the missing runtime-application guidance for file-based selection. A successful write to the canonical user config now returns a structured restart_hint and text guidance to run vinpst daemon restart if the daemon is already running. The CLI deliberately does not call the additive SetCaptureDevice D-Bus extension after rewriting the file: file mutation and live runtime mutation remain separate authorities, while the daemon D-Bus method continues to provide same-owner next-recording switching for GUI/live-control surfaces.

Vinpst intentionally requires --in-place or --output for device use instead of silently mutating the user config as frozen does. This matches the rewrite-wide explicit-mutation policy, preserves backup/atomic-write behavior, allows deterministic dry-run and offline config generation, and does not remove the familiar device use task.

Deterministic evidence includes the full PipeWire-feature audio_devices integration suite (19 tests), the exact device ls parser compatibility test, canonical in-place restart-hint coverage, unavailable-PipeWire best-effort selection coverage, and strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy with and without pipewire-backend.

audits.title: CLI LLM provider and text-adapter workflows
notes: Frozen owns LLM-provider and LLM-adapter commands in the same llm_actions/register_llm files, so this audit intentionally keeps them in one non-overlapping unit. The familiar provider surface remains available as llm list/ls, add, edit/e, remove/rm, and test. The familiar adapter surface remains available as adapter list/ls -a/--available, registry add (accepted as an alias of the clearer install command), start, and stop; Vinpst adds custom create/edit/remove, runtime status, dry-run/JSON, and safer explicit write targets.

LLM mutation semantics preserve the meaningful frozen behavior while strengthening validation. Provider ids/base URLs are trimmed and validated, extra_body must be an object, and the frozen edit -e/--extra-body {} form remains accepted and persists an empty object. Vinpst intentionally rejects no-op edits and uses explicit --clear-* controls for optional scalar fields instead of treating ambiguous empty strings as mutation instructions. Provider removal also clears scene provider/model bindings that would otherwise dangle, and all writes use the shared validated backup/atomic persistence path.

LLM list output intentionally minimizes credentials and endpoints more aggressively than frozen. Frozen JSON returns raw base_url plus an empty api_key placeholder and text prints raw base_url plus a partially masked key; Vinpst reports configuration booleans/model metadata in JSON, redacts URL diagnostics in text, and never emits configured API-key material. Adapter installed-list JSON likewise reports command/argument/environment counts and configured-state flags rather than frozen raw command, args, and env values. Runtime adapter state moved to the daemon-authoritative adapter status surface instead of inferring running state from local process metadata.

vinpst llm test is an intentional product divergence from frozen. Frozen performs a fixed-10-second GET of the OpenAI-compatible /models endpoint and reports model ids. Vinpst exercises the actual production non-streaming /chat/completions text-processing path, with the same scene timeout/request builder/response parser used by runtime post-processing, plus a no-network --dry-run and structural credential/URL redaction. The text architecture and live validation documents explicitly use vinpst llm test as the production authenticated chat request/result boundary, so reverting it to /models would reduce coverage of the user-visible path.

Adapter registry installation preserves short-id resolution, live registry/i18n metadata, script materialization, and configuration publication while adding staging, dry-run, explicit write targets, required/optional environment reporting, and refusal to replace user-defined adapters with managed content. Start/stop resolve configured ids (or registry short ids when explicitly supplied) before invoking the stable StartAdapter/StopAdapter D-Bus methods; status is an additive daemon-authoritative diagnostic command.

Deterministic evidence includes the existing llm_adapter suite for secret-free LLM/adapter listing, registry installation, selector resolution, StartAdapter/StopAdapter plans, mutation validation, redacted LLM request plans, the legacy 4000 ms text-scene timeout, and removal safety. This audit additionally pins frozen llm ls/e/rm and adapter ls -a/add parser forms plus the frozen-compatible llm edit --extra-body {} persistence behavior; strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy remains green.

audits.title: CLI recognition-scene workflows
notes: The frozen scene task surface remains available as scene list/ls, add, use, remove/rm, and edit/e. Vinpst keeps its clearer positional add ID and explicit mutation targets, but now also accepts the frozen --id form plus -l/--label, -t/--prompt, -p/--provider, -m/--model, -c/--candidates, and --timeout spellings as aliases of the typed current options. Current clear-* edit switches, dry-run/JSON, backups, and offline --output remain additive.

Fixed a behavioral default regression in scene add. Frozen custom scenes start with candidate_count=1; the rewrite CLI had defaulted to 0, which can skip candidate post-processing entirely. Vinpst scene add now defaults candidate_count to 1 again. Frozen writes timeout_ms=4000 on add, while Vinpst intentionally omits the field and relies on SceneDefinition::effective_timeout_ms()=4000; the runtime deadline is therefore equivalent without serializing a redundant legacy default.

Frozen permits an omitted or explicitly empty scene label and DisplayLabel then falls back to the builtin label or scene id. Vinpst typed config rejects empty labels globally, so the CLI preserves the user-visible frozen behavior by normalizing an omitted/empty custom label to the scene id rather than weakening config validation. Scene list JSON/text also uses display-label fallback semantics, including builtin labels, so imported legacy empty-label data remains presented sensibly where it can be loaded.

Scene remove/use constraints align: frozen RemoveScene(force=false) and Vinpst both reject built-in scenes and the active scene, while scene use requires an existing scene. Vinpst continues to reject no-op edit requests and represents cleared optional prompt/provider/model/timeout fields by omission through explicit --clear-* controls instead of frozen empty-string storage; this is the rewrite typed-schema policy rather than a missing user task.

Vinpst intentionally requires --in-place or --output for scene mutations instead of silently writing the canonical config. This preserves the rewrite-wide safe mutation/backup policy. Neither frozen scene CLI nor current file-based scene CLI performs an implicit daemon runtime mutation after writing; live scene selection remains owned by the daemon/Fcitx typed D-Bus surfaces audited separately.

Deterministic evidence includes the scene integration suite, which now pins --id scene creation with an omitted label, candidate_count=1, omitted serialized timeout, and list-time label fallback, plus an exact parser test for the frozen add/edit short-option and legacy long-option forms. Strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy remains green.

audits.title: CLI recording control workflows
notes: The frozen recording task surface remains available as recording/rec start, stop, and toggle. Vinpst adds recording status plus hidden selected-text command-mode and dry-run controls, but these do not replace the familiar tasks. Restored the frozen -s/--scene spelling on stop and toggle; the user-facing help now states that an omitted scene means the active scene.

Fixed a runtime-control regression: frozen EnsureDaemon probes org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner before every start/stop/toggle call, so recording control never activates a stopped daemon. Vinpst now shares one non-activating daemon_name_has_owner helper across recording, ASR config reload, and daemon-removal verification; recording start/stop/toggle and the additive status command all fail with Daemon is not running when no owner exists instead of constructing an activating service call.

Restored the frozen toggle state policy before issuing a mutating call. recording toggles recording -> stop and idle -> start, rejects inferring/postprocessing as busy, and rejects error explicitly. Unknown wire strings intentionally use ServiceStatus::parse_legacy_wire and therefore fall back to idle/start exactly like the frozen status conversion semantics instead of silently broadening the strict parser used elsewhere.

Frozen resolves an omitted stop/toggle scene in the CLI by re-reading the on-disk config and sending its active scene id. Vinpst deliberately sends the empty legacy sentinel and lets the already-running daemon resolve the active scene from its authoritative runtime config. This avoids a stale CLI-side config read while preserving the same user result.

Stop-result handling is an intentional Rust-service extension. Frozen StopRecording is a successful/failed void control call and the CLI prints only the action/scene. The audited Vinpst D-Bus contract synchronously returns the final recognition payload; the CLI therefore reports committed text/candidate metadata after stop while retaining the same scene control semantics.

Frozen command-local JSON failures print {ok:false,error} before returning exit 1. Vinpst currently uses the rewrite-wide anyhow stderr/nonzero error path for live command failures even when JSON output was requested. This audit does not add a recording-only exit/error framework; the remaining cross-command formatter/error-shape question stays with the pending CLI utility/runtime audit rather than duplicating infrastructure here.

Deterministic evidence includes the existing recording integration tests, an exact rec stop/toggle -s parser compatibility test, a pure toggle-state regression test covering idle/recording/inferring/postprocessing/error/unknown status, strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy, and a private-session-bus smoke with an observable activation service proving recording start and status fail without ever activating org.fcitx.Vinpst.

audits.title: CLI daemon lifecycle, status, and journal workflows
notes: The frozen user tasks remain available as daemon status, start, stop, restart, and log. Vinpst adds reload-asr plus hidden installation/handoff/removal controls, richer JSON diagnostics, owner/procfs inspection, and dry-run plans without removing the familiar lifecycle surface.

Fixed daemon log parity. The rewrite had lost -f/--follow and had no frozen-equivalent default tail; log now defaults to the last 100 entries and accepts -n/--lines plus -f/--follow. Follow uses an inherited-stdio Command::status execution path rather than the ordinary captured Command::output runner, so journal entries are actually streamed to the terminal instead of buffered until a never-ending follow exits. Live --follow is intentionally rejected with JSON output because the unbounded journal stream and one JSON document cannot safely share stdout; --follow --dry-run --json remains available for plan inspection.

Fixed a shell-contract regression in stop/restart/log. The rewrite previously printed a structured result with ok=false when systemctl/journalctl was missing or returned nonzero but still exited 0. The CLI now preserves the existing human/JSON diagnostic payload and then returns a command failure, so scripts receive a nonzero process status like frozen upstream. Tests cover missing executables and explicit child exit 1 for stop, restart, and log.

daemon start is an intentional Vinpst lifecycle divergence. Frozen starts the user systemd unit directly; current start triggers org.fcitx.Vinpst through the installed D-Bus activation service and reports the resulting live status/owner. The dry-run contract explicitly identifies dbus-service-activation/GetStatus, and the installed activation-owner smoke proves that the first status/start-style service call activates the expected installed daemon and reports its owner/runtime. This supports direct D-Bus activation from Fcitx and avoids making systemd the only startup authority.

daemon status intentionally queries the live service and can therefore activate a stopped daemon, unlike frozen IsDaemonRunning plus GetStatus. Owner diagnostics are deliberately collected after the first successful service method so the initial activation-backed query reports the new PID/executable rather than a pre-activation null owner. It also reports ASR readiness, runtime/text-adapter state, and stale-binary handoff guidance. Recording control retains the separately audited non-activating owner-probe behavior; status is the explicit lifecycle/diagnostic activation surface.

daemon stop/restart preserve the frozen user-systemd tasks through the shared vinpst-daemon-control command builder. Flatpak execution intentionally wraps host systemctl/journalctl with flatpak-spawn and uses the host journal filter, with exact argv tests; non-sandboxed operation still targets vinpst-daemon.service. The shared systemd runner itself remains supporting here and stays pending for the dedicated frozen cli/runtime/systemd_client audit.

Current daemon log rejects --lines 0 instead of passing an ambiguous zero tail to journalctl, a small fail-closed validation improvement. Human output also suppresses low-level tool plumbing while JSON keeps command/tool/sandbox/fallback diagnostics for troubleshooting. Deterministic evidence includes daemon start/status dry-run plans, the installed activation-owner smoke, exact Flatpak wrappers, default/follow journal tests, child-failure exit propagation, vinpst-daemon-control tests, and strict all-target Clippy for both crates.

audits.title: Shared user-systemd command construction and execution
notes: Frozen systemd_client combines systemctl lifecycle execution, journalctl command construction/capture, Flatpak host wrapping, restart/start failure diagnosis, and notification dispatch. Vinpst intentionally splits those responsibilities: vinpst-daemon-control owns shell-free user-systemd argv construction plus captured/streaming execution, CLI sandbox/service code owns journal filters and user-facing service diagnostics, daemon error_info owns runtime error classification, and daemon start moved to D-Bus activation.

The shared Rust command contract matches the frozen native and sandboxed stop/restart tasks: systemctl --user stop/restart vinpst-daemon.service is emitted without a shell, and Flatpak wraps the target with flatpak-spawn --host while preserving executable overrides. Vinpst additionally centralizes disable --now, daemon-reload, and MainPID probes for installation/handoff/removal workflows; these are additive service-management primitives rather than frozen parity requirements.

Execution semantics preserve child status and spawn failures without exposing command arguments through Debug. The captured runner uses Command::output for finite systemctl/journalctl-style operations; the streaming runner added during daemon-log parity uses inherited stdio and Command::status, preserving success/failure status without buffering output. Unit tests now pin both success and exit-1 streaming outcomes, while CLI integration tests pin that service failures propagate a nonzero process status.

SystemctlStart/SystemctlStartWithDiagnostics are intentionally absent from the shared action enum because Vinpst startup authority is D-Bus activation rather than direct systemctl start. The separately audited daemon CLI dry-run and installed activation-owner smoke prove this product contract. Stop and restart remain systemd user-service operations because they intentionally control the existing service owner/lifecycle rather than request activation.

Frozen JournalctlLogs/JournalctlLogsText moved upward rather than disappearing: CLI sandbox/service code builds the native unit or Flatpak-host journal filter, applies the frozen -n tail and -f follow semantics, and uses captured or streaming execution as appropriate. The sandbox source remains supporting here because it also owns broader Flatpak packaging/permission policy and is reserved for its own frozen common/utils/sandbox audit.

Frozen restart/start diagnostics automatically append the last 20 journal lines, classify actionable text, and emit an ErrorInfo notification. Vinpst deliberately does not auto-dump journal content from the shared systemd layer: systemctl stdout/stderr and structured fallback steps remain available, users opt into bounded daemon log output, and daemon-originated error classification stays with the daemon notification authority. This avoids coupling the low-level runner to D-Bus/error taxonomy and reduces accidental disclosure of provider/path details in control-command failures.

Deterministic evidence includes exact native stop/restart argv, Flatpak host-wrapped argv with tool overrides, captured-output privacy behavior, streaming success/failure status tests, daemon CLI journal/failure integration tests, and strict all-target vinpst-daemon-control Clippy.

audits.title: CLI D-Bus control transport and deadlines
notes: Frozen dbus_client is one sd-bus wrapper for daemon ownership/status, ASR state/reload, recording start/stop, adapter lifecycle, and Fcitx notification calls. Vinpst intentionally distributes those typed calls across daemon-control, recording, and adapter modules while keeping one shared connection/proxy boundary for short control operations.

Fixed a transport deadline regression. Frozen DbusClient sets kDbusCallTimeoutUsec to five seconds on its user bus, while zbus Connection::session() leaves method_timeout unset. Vinpst now builds short CLI control connections with an explicit five-second method timeout, covering NameHasOwner, status/backend/runtime queries, ASR reload, recording start/status, and adapter lifecycle/status. A private-session test asserts the live zbus connection carries exactly that timeout.

StopRecording deliberately remains outside the five-second connection. Frozen StopRecording is an immediate acknowledgement whose result is delivered asynchronously, but the audited Rust service synchronously returns the final recognition payload after ASR and optional text processing. The CLI therefore bounds the preceding non-activating owner/status control calls while allowing the synchronous final stop operation to complete according to the recognition backend contract.

Activation remains caller-specific rather than hidden inside the transport. Recording controls and canonical ASR config writes first use NameHasOwner and do not activate an absent daemon; the existing private-session smokes prove both boundaries. Adapter start/stop directly address the service and may activate it as frozen did. Vinpst daemon status/start intentionally use D-Bus activation and were already recorded in CLI-DAEMON-001.

Frozen Notify is only consumed by the systemctl start/restart failure path. CLI-SYSTEMD-RUNTIME-001 intentionally keeps those failures as structured control diagnostics plus opt-in bounded journal inspection instead of automatically scraping journal text, classifying it, and sending a notifier call. This audit therefore does not add an otherwise-unused CLI notifier transport solely for shape parity.

Wire method names and ASR backend tuple compatibility are owned by the protocol/service audits. Vinpst adds richer daemon runtime/text-adapter status queries and a standalone daemon reload-asr command without changing the frozen method shapes needed by existing config, recording, or adapter tasks. Typed zbus/anyhow errors replace the frozen bool plus optional error-string API.

Deterministic evidence includes the private-bus five-second connection assertion, recording no-activation smoke, canonical ASR write/reload smoke, focused recording/adapter/reload tests, and strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy.

audits.title: CLI human and JSON output formatting boundary
notes: Frozen formatter is a shared polymorphic TextFormatter/JsonFormatter for tables, key/value pairs, success, error, warning, info, and arbitrary JSON. Vinpst intentionally keeps formatting close to typed command outcomes instead of routing every domain through one formatter object; this lets each user task expose a stable structured document rather than reducing all output to generic table/status records.

Fixed the cross-command runtime-error gap. Frozen JsonFormatter::PrintError writes a compact {status:error,message} object to stderr when -j/--json is active, while Vinpst previously let anyhow termination print plain Error: text even for JSON-mode runtime failures. The CLI now detects either root or command-local -j/--json before the -- argument delimiter and emits the same generic JSON error shape on stderr while preserving a nonzero process status.

Text-mode runtime errors retain the existing anyhow diagnostic chain and Error: prefix. Parser-library errors still occur before action dispatch and remain Clap-owned as recorded in CLI-ROOT-001, matching the frozen separation where CLI11 parse failures also bypass Formatter action output.

Frozen action code sometimes bypasses JsonFormatter::PrintError and explicitly prints command-specific JSON such as recording {ok:false,error}; those schemas are action contracts rather than formatter behavior. Vinpst likewise keeps richer per-command success/failure documents, including daemon service diagnostics, under their already-audited domain units instead of forcing them into the generic status/message envelope.

Vinpst intentionally omits frozen ANSI color/bold decoration and generic display-width table padding. Human command tables use simple domain-specific text/tabular layouts, while --json is the machine-readable surface. This keeps the user interface plain and avoids terminal escape handling without dropping data. Domain warnings also remain owned by their command outcomes rather than introducing a second global formatter abstraction.

Deterministic evidence includes pure argv JSON-mode detection before/after subcommands and the -- delimiter, process-level tests for local and root JSON runtime failures, a text-mode failure regression, the existing root global-JSON propagation tests, and strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy.

audits.title: CLI editor command parsing and launch policy
notes: Frozen OpenInEditor selects VISUAL, then EDITOR, then vi; parses a small shell-like command grammar into direct argv; appends the file path; executes with execvp rather than a shell; waits for completion; and propagates the editor exit status. Vinpst keeps direct Command argv execution and adds explicit --editor plus VINPST_*_EDITOR overrides ahead of that legacy fallback chain.

Fixed the Rust rewrite command parser. config/hotword and provider script editing previously used split_whitespace(), which broke quoted editor arguments and escaped spaces. A shared vinpst-process parse_command_argv state machine now preserves the frozen single-quote, double-quote, backslash, and ASCII-whitespace rules while deliberately performing no shell expansion or operator evaluation. Empty commands and unterminated quote/escape syntax fail before process launch.

Fixed config/hotword environment priority and fallback. After their explicit/Vinpst-specific override, both now select VISUAL before EDITOR and fall back to vi, matching frozen behavior. Provider editing already had explicit -> VINPST_PROVIDER_EDITOR -> VISUAL -> EDITOR -> vi selection and now shares the corrected argv parser. CLI help text reflects the actual order.

Vinpst config editing intentionally strengthens frozen direct-file editing: it edits a temporary copy, parses and validates edited core JSON, preserves an existing config backup, and atomically writes the accepted result. Invalid editor output or a failing editor cannot overwrite the live config. Provider-script and hotword editing remain direct existing-file edits, matching their frozen task shape.

Process launch remains shell-free across all three editor surfaces, so quotes affect argv grouping only and cannot introduce shell evaluation. Vinpst reports typed spawn/parse/exit failures with more context than frozen integer -1 while preserving nonzero editor status as command failure.

Deterministic evidence includes shared parser quote/escape and malformed-command tests, provider editor priority/default and quoted-argv tests, process-level config/hotword VISUAL-over-EDITOR dry-runs with quoted arguments, existing real editor success/failure tests, and strict all-target Clippy for vinpst-process, vinpst-registry, and vinpst-cli.

audits.title: CLI config and scene glue helpers
notes: Frozen cli_helpers.h is glue rather than a standalone runtime module: SaveConfigOrFail writes the canonical CoreConfig and prints one generic error; ToSceneConfig/FromSceneConfig copy the scene fields into the scene helper type; ResolveSceneId reloads CoreConfig and resolves an empty explicit id to the configured active scene.

Vinpst deliberately has no one-to-one helper file. Typed VinpstConfig owns the scene representation directly, so no lossy CoreConfig-to-scene projection/copy-back pair is needed. Scene list/add/use/remove/edit operate on the same typed document validated by vinpst-config.

Config persistence is intentionally safer and more explicit than frozen SaveConfigOrFail. User-facing mutations select --in-place or --output, validate the complete derived document, preserve backups for in-place writes, and use atomic publication helpers; canonical ASR mutations additionally reload an already-running daemon without activating an absent one. Those behaviors are owned by the previously audited config/ASR/scene/device/LLM units rather than duplicated in a generic bool helper.

Recording scene resolution intentionally moved to the daemon authority. The CLI preserves an explicit scene id, but an omitted/empty scene reaches Start/StopRecording as empty and the daemon resolves it against its effective active configuration. This avoids the frozen race where the CLI independently reloads disk config immediately before calling a daemon that may hold a different runtime generation. CLI-RECORDING-001 and the private-bus recording gates cover that task behavior.
No production change is required for this glue-only unit; reproducing the header would reintroduce duplicate config ownership and scene translation state without adding a user capability.

audits.title: CLI resource display, selector, and TTY progress context
notes: Frozen resource_utils centralizes user-facing short-id selection, localized title/description metadata, optional README terminal links, registry-backed selector resolution, and model/script display-map fetching. CliContext supplies the json_output and stdout-is-a-TTY bits used by that display layer and model download progress. Vinpst moves typed display and selector behavior onto live registry entries while command modules own their task-specific text/JSON documents.

Fixed live resource display-id parity. Live models and scripts now expose display_id(), preferring a non-empty registry short id and falling back to the stable machine id. Live model JSON now publishes the human selector as id while retaining machine_id and short_id explicitly; model/provider/adapter live text lists likewise show short ids. Provider/adapter JSON already used the short selector and now shares the same typed helper.

Selector semantics remain at least as strict as frozen behavior. Live model lookup accepts exact full id or short id and registry validation rejects duplicate short ids; script registry validation likewise rejects duplicate selectors and resolves full id or short id within the requested kind. Vinpst therefore does not need a second CLI-only ResolveSelector template to recreate the same lookup state.

Vinpst intentionally does not fetch remote registries merely to decorate already-configured local provider/adapter lists or registry-independent installed-model scans. Those offline surfaces keep their known local identifiers and persisted metadata; commands that need registry short-id resolution take an explicit/live registry path. This avoids turning local inspection into a hidden network dependency while preserving short-id UX on live registry tasks.

Frozen FormatTerminalLink emits OSC 8 links only on a TTY. Vinpst intentionally keeps human output escape-free and omits README link columns from compact text tables; readme_url remains available in structured live provider/adapter JSON. This matches the formatter audit decision to keep the terminal UI simple without losing machine-readable resource metadata.

Fixed the missing model-install progress path. Frozen model add reports download progress to stderr using stdout TTY state, with live TTY refreshes and ten-percent non-TTY buckets. Vinpst already emitted typed RegistryOperationProgress events but the CLI used the no-op install wrapper. Model install now attaches a RegistryOperationControl reporter: TTY sessions receive a simple live percentage, non-TTY sessions receive increasing ten-percent lines, successful installs finish at 100%, and JSON stdout remains a single document. The simpler percentage display deliberately omits the frozen decorative bar/speed calculation while restoring essential long-running feedback.

Deterministic evidence includes live model/provider/adapter short-id text/JSON tests, registry title fallback tests, a local-HTTP model install proving non-TTY stderr reaches 100% while stdout JSON remains parseable, and strict all-target Clippy for vinpst-cli and vinpst-registry.

audits.title: Terminal model download progress presentation
notes: Frozen ProgressBar is used only by CLI model installation. It writes progress to stderr, uses stdout TTY state to select an in-place display versus line-oriented output, clamps percentages to 100, emits non-TTY progress only when a new ten-percent bucket is crossed, and finishes with a newline or explicit 100 percent line.

The current CLI now consumes RegistryOperationProgress::Downloading through RegistryOperationControl for the same model-install task. Non-TTY output uses increasing ten-percent stderr lines and successful completion reaches 100 percent; TTY output refreshes one stderr line in place. The local-HTTP install regression proves progress remains separate from the single JSON stdout document.

Vinpst intentionally keeps the TTY presentation simpler: it reports the percentage without reproducing the frozen twenty-character ASCII bar or speed suffix. The typed registry progress event does not currently carry a transfer-rate estimate, and adding presentation-only rate bookkeeping would not improve correctness. Essential long-running feedback and stream separation are preserved.

The current typed progress/cancellation model is intentionally kept in vinpst-registry rather than introducing a second generic terminal progress class. The registry operation module remains unclaimed here because its broader cancellation and staging semantics belong to downloader/registry audits.

audits.title: Registry HTTP text and asset downloader boundary
notes: Frozen Downloader tries candidate URLs in order, defaults to a 30-second request timeout, follows redirects, accepts only final HTTP 200 for http/https, supports optional text-size limits and file progress, removes a failed file destination before trying the next URL, and reports the final effective URL plus sanitized failure state. Registry model/script text callers use 30 seconds and 4 MiB; model assets use 600 seconds and script assets 120 seconds.

Fixed the Rust HTTP status boundary. Reqwest text and asset sources previously accepted every 2xx response through StatusCode::is_success(), so a 206 partial response could be treated as a complete asset and even pass checksum if the partial bytes matched the expected small fixture. Both sources now require StatusCode::OK exactly, matching frozen DownloadText/DownloadFile. Local HTTP regressions prove 206 is rejected for both text and asset paths and failed asset staging leaves no published or temporary file.

Fixed the missing bounded-text contract. ReqwestRegistryTextSource now accepts an explicit maximum response size; it rejects an oversized Content-Length before buffering and also reads at most max+1 when the server omits a trustworthy length, so the limit cannot be bypassed with connection-close framing. Production model/provider/adapter registry fetches in CLI and GUI now use the frozen 30-second/4-MiB boundary. Registry JSON also fails closed on invalid UTF-8 instead of lossy decoding.

Fixed timeout parity for generic and model downloads. ReqwestRegistryTextSource::new and ReqwestRegistryAssetSource::new now carry the frozen 30-second default rather than leaving timeout behavior to reqwest. CLI and GUI model asset installs now use 600 seconds; script assets remain at their already-correct 120 seconds. The exact frozen i18n 20-second/1-MiB policy is intentionally deferred to the dedicated registry-i18n audit because current i18n layering has its own source construction.

Mirror fallback is split between typed layers rather than one Downloader class: fetch_registry_text_from_mirrors preserves ordered text fallback, while stage_planned_asset_controlled preserves ordered asset fallback. The Rust asset staging boundary is stronger than frozen direct destination writes: every attempt uses a caller-owned temporary path, cancellation and transport/checksum failures remove partial files, checksum verification happens before publication, and the final tree/file move is handled by the registry staging/materialization contract.

Redirect following remains enabled through reqwest default policy, with reqwest additionally bounding redirect count. Frozen exposes follow_redirects as a generic option but no audited production caller disables it, so a separate disable switch is not reproduced. The Rust source API also does not expose the final effective URL; audited resource/i18n resolution is based on configured registry bases rather than a downloader redirect result, so no user-visible dependency on that field was found.

Rust downloader diagnostics intentionally redact request URLs, headers, response bodies, and transport internals more aggressively than frozen curl error strings. Typed RegistryOperationProgress supplies byte counts/cancellation for asset downloads; presentation differences such as speed calculation are recorded separately in DOWNLOAD-PROGRESS-001.

Deterministic evidence includes exact-200 text/asset local-HTTP tests, Content-Length and lengthless streamed-body limit tests, existing mirror-fallback/timeout/checksum/temp-cleanup/cancellation tests, full vinpst-registry/vinpst-cli/vinpst-gui suites, and strict all-target Clippy for all three crates.

audits.title: Registry locale detection and layered i18n loading
notes: Frozen registry i18n normalizes locale names, detects the preferred locale from LANGUAGE/LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES/LANG, fetches preferred then en_US fallback translation maps from all configured registry mirrors with a 20-second/1-MiB downloader boundary, merges fallback then preferred, and finally lets i18n.local.json override both. Remote failure is nonfatal to catalog loading.

Fixed translation parsing parity. LiveRegistryI18n previously deserialized directly into BTreeMap<String,String>, so any non-string JSON value rejected the whole layer. It now requires an object but inserts only string-valued members and ignores numbers, booleans, arrays, and nested objects like the frozen ParseI18nJson helper. Malformed JSON and non-object roots still fail closed.

Fixed the remote i18n transport policy. CLI and GUI now use a dedicated 20-second/1-MiB ReqwestRegistryTextSource for production remote translations rather than the CLI 10-second unlimited source or the GUI 30-second/4-MiB registry-index source. DOWNLOADER-001 provides exact-HTTP-200 and bounded-body enforcement underneath this call site.

Fixed mirror independence. Translation lookup now walks every configured registry base for each locale instead of deriving one i18n base from whichever mirror happened to serve the registry index. This restores the frozen ResolveRegistryI18nUrls behavior and allows a registry index from one mirror to use translations from another. An explicit local --registry fixture intentionally disables implicit remote i18n unless an explicit i18n file is supplied, preserving deterministic offline test/user behavior.

Fixed fetch order to preferred locale first and en_US fallback second while preserving merge precedence fallback < preferred < local. If one mirror transport request fails the next mirror is tried; once a mirror returns a body, parse success/failure decides that locale layer exactly as in frozen FetchText followed by ParseI18nJson rather than silently skipping a malformed successful response to another mirror.

Current locale normalization remains slightly more defensive by trimming surrounding whitespace before applying the frozen colon/encoding/modifier/hyphen/C/POSIX/zh/en rules. LiveRegistryI18n::get also treats whitespace-only translations as absent, while frozen only treats an empty string as absent. Both are intentional fail-soft cleanup that do not remove a valid translation value.

The CLI keeps richer per-layer diagnostics and a deterministic explicit i18n file override; malformed local overrides are nonfatal and cannot erase usable remote layers. GUI uses the same preferred/fallback map semantics but keeps presentation ownership in its catalog modules.

Frozen cached preferred/fallback i18n loading and stale-cache policy are not claimed by this unit. common/registry/registry_cache.* remains pending and is the next audit target so cache freshness, stale fallback, and atomic cache publication can be compared without duplicating ownership here.

Deterministic evidence includes mixed-value i18n parsing, preferred-before-fallback layer ordering, independent multi-mirror translation fallback, malformed local override recovery, GUI registry-index/i18n mirror independence, existing locale normalization tests, and strict all-target Clippy for vinpst-registry, vinpst-cli, and vinpst-gui.

audits.title: Live registry text cache and stale fallback
notes: Frozen RegistryCache fetches ordered registry URLs, atomically publishes each successful text download to a fixed cache file, and only when all fresh transport attempts fail falls back to the stale cached text. Cache hits retain the fresh-download failure for a caller warning. There is no TTL gate: any readable stale cache may recover an offline fetch.

Fixed a production wiring gap. The Rust RegistryTextCache previously existed only around the older RegistryIndex helper/tests and was not used by live models, providers, adapters, or registry i18n. A schema-neutral fetch_registry_text_with_cache primitive now owns fresh mirror fallback, atomic text publication, stale text recovery, used_cache state, and sanitized fallback classification while each live parser continues to own its own schema.

Restored the frozen cache layout under Vinpst identity: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/fcitx-vinpst/registry/models.json, providers.json, adapters.json, and i18n/<locale>.json, with HOME/.cache fallback through the existing CLI/GUI cache-root helpers. Locale cache filenames are additionally sanitized against path separators and unusual characters.

CLI live model/provider/adapter catalogs and installs now use these cache paths whenever the user did not supply an explicit local --registry file. Registry JSON source diagnostics distinguish fresh http from cache, preserve used_cache and a sanitized fallback_error, and human output emits a concise cached-registry warning without leaking configured mirror URLs or credentials.

CLI preferred/fallback i18n layers now independently cache each normalized locale with the frozen 20-second/1-MiB request policy from REGISTRY-I18N-001. A process-level test seeds isolated models.json and zh_CN.json cache files, points the configured mirror at a refused localhost endpoint, and proves vinpst model list still returns localized JSON with both source kinds reported as cache.

GUI model browsing, model install/selection resolution, provider/adapter browsing, and managed script preparation now use the same stale-cache primitive. Deterministic GUI tests prove a model registry remains available after the source goes offline and that a provider catalog plus its en_US translation remains usable after both registry and i18n network sources disappear.

Aligned successful-body semantics while connecting the cache. Transport errors advance to later mirrors, but once a mirror returns a body that body is parsed; malformed successful JSON is an error rather than silently trying a later mirror. This matches frozen DownloadText followed by parser behavior and removes the previous GUI-only malformed-mirror fallback.

Fresh successful transport text is cached before the live schema parser runs, matching frozen RegistryCache ordering. Therefore a malformed HTTP-200 body may replace the previous cache before parse failure; parse-before-publication would be a separate hardening change rather than claimed parity here.

Atomic cache publication creates parent directories, writes a same-directory temporary file, renames over the target, and now removes partial temporary files on both write and rename failure. Existing tests also prove an orphaned temporary file is never mistaken for a valid cache entry.

Test-only injected-source helpers may deliberately bypass cache so unit fixtures remain deterministic; all production Reqwest live registry and i18n entry points route through cached helpers. Deterministic evidence includes raw fresh/stale cache tests, cache-path tests, existing atomic/stale/partial-temp tests, CLI offline process proof, GUI offline model/provider+i18n proofs, malformed-success rejection, and strict all-target Clippy for registry/CLI/GUI.

audits.title: Live registry fetch orchestration and i18n cache refresh
notes: Frozen FetchRegistryText composes downloader/cache behavior with two policies above RegistryCache: a stale registry hit emits a cached-registry warning and deliberately skips i18n refresh, while a fresh registry download best-effort refreshes the detected preferred locale cache and then en_US when distinct.

Restored that missing orchestration in a dedicated vinpst-registry live_fetch module. The production helper owns the frozen 30-second/4-MiB registry source and 20-second/1-MiB i18n source, reuses the cache primitive from REGISTRY-CACHE-001, and returns raw registry text plus sanitized warning classifications without taking ownership of model/script schemas.

A fresh registry fetch now primes preferred/en_US i18n caches for every config-aware remote registry operation, not only catalog pages. This closes prior gaps in CLI provider/adapter install and remote resolution paths plus GUI model selection/install and managed provider/adapter preparation, so a later offline UI can retain translations even when the triggering action did not itself render localized metadata.

A stale registry fallback does not perform new i18n requests, matching frozen behavior. The shared deterministic test seeds a stale models.json cache, forces registry transport failure, proves the i18n source receives zero requests, and preserves a warning shaped as using cached <registry> because download failed.

I18n refresh failures remain nonfatal. Fresh preferred/en_US responses atomically update their locale caches; unavailable locales without cache are silently ignored; stale locale fallback remains usable and produces a sanitized warning. The high-level helper does not parse i18n JSON during refresh, matching the frozen common fetch boundary.

CLI remote model/provider/adapter loaders now route through the shared high-level helper instead of constructing their own registry HTTP source. Their structured registry_source keeps http/cache source metadata and now carries the shared warning list; human catalog output prints these warnings while retaining the simpler Vinpst text presentation.

GUI model registry resolution and script preparation route through the injectable high-level helper with separate registry and i18n sources, preserving deterministic tests while matching production request limits. A focused GUI test proves a model-registry-only fetch primes en_US i18n cache before any catalog presentation explicitly loads translations.

Explicit local registry files continue to bypass network/cache refresh, and the legacy no-CoreConfig frozen model overload likewise has no direct Vinpst equivalent requiring refresh because current user-facing remote operations always have typed RegistryConfig context.

Frozen resolved_registry_url may contain the downloader final redirect URL or a cache path, but source search found no CLI/GUI consumer using it to resolve assets or other behavior. Current diagnostics retain the attempted fresh mirror URL (or cache path) rather than expanding the RegistryTextSource trait solely for final-redirect precision; this is an intentional diagnostic-only simplification.

The module deliberately exports only the high-level fetch functions and result type; internal locale-refresh helpers remain private to avoid growing a second public registry API surface. Evidence includes four shared orchestration tests, GUI fresh-i18n-prefetch proof, existing stale-cache process/GUI proofs, and strict all-target Clippy for registry, CLI, and GUI.

audits.title: Live model registry parsing and managed model installation
notes: Frozen registry_models owns live model parsing, ordered registry fetch, model selection by stable id, 600-second archive download with URL fallback, optional SHA-256 verification, libarchive extraction with secure-path flags, single-top-directory flattening, runtime metadata publication, replacement backup/rollback, and the model repository destination mapping.

The Rust rewrite splits those responsibilities across typed live schema, the already-audited downloader/cache/fetch boundaries, archive/checksum staging, install orchestration, materialization, and managed/installed model owners. This audit claims only the still-unowned archive/checksum/install/materialize/staging modules; live.rs, asset.rs, installed.rs, and managed.rs retain their earlier owners and are supporting evidence rather than double-counted here.

Core install behavior is preserved. Candidate archive URLs are attempted in order, model downloads use the frozen 600-second production timeout from DOWNLOADER-001, declared SHA-256 is verified before extraction, missing SHA-256 remains accepted at runtime with an explicit Missing checksum state, a single archive root is flattened, typed runtime metadata is written in the staged tree, and only then is the completed model published.

Added end-to-end evidence that a repeated model install replaces an existing managed model only after staging completes, updates model files and metadata together, removes old-only files, and leaves no replacement backup behind. Lower-level materialization tests already cover publish rollback and cross-filesystem copy-then-rename publication.

Added end-to-end evidence for the frozen optional-checksum runtime behavior: a model entry without sha256 still installs successfully and reports AssetChecksumStatus::Missing. The separate upstream registry contribution contract nevertheless lists sha256 as required, and the current public registry snapshot has seven version-2 model entries, all with 64-character SHA-256 values and complete runtime metadata.

The current live parser is deliberately fail-closed where frozen parsing is permissive: malformed/empty items, duplicate ids/short ids, invalid checksums, and invalid version fail the document instead of silently dropping entries. This matches the published registry contract and prevents a partially malformed signed/trusted catalog from changing what resources the user sees.

Archive support is intentionally narrower and safer than frozen libarchive format-all extraction. Current extraction accepts plain tar, tar.zst, tar.bz2, and tbz2 only; it rejects links, traversal, absolute/backslash paths, and unknown entry kinds inside a private staging tree. The current upstream public model registry was checked during this audit and all seven downloadable archives are tar.bz2, so this whitelist covers the actual published resource set. Gzip/xz/zip wrappers remain an explicit future extension in registry-contract.md rather than silently expanding the attack surface.

The frozen fallback archive filename `<model-id>.tar.gz` is not reproduced for URL paths without a filename. Current installation requires the first URL to expose a supported archive filename because wrapper selection is explicit and suffix-based. Published model URLs all expose tar.bz2 filenames, so this is an intentional contract tightening rather than a present resource gap.

Runtime metadata uses the Vinpst-owned `vinpst-model.json` identity instead of frozen `vinput-model.json`. Missing runtime metadata is rejected by install orchestration instead of producing an unusable metadata-less managed model; the upstream contribution guide lists vinput_model as required for every local ASR model.

Current publication is stronger than frozen in several ways retained intentionally: cooperative cancellation spans download/extract/publish, extraction happens in a validated temporary tree, existing targets are backed up and rolled back on publish failure, cross-filesystem targets use copy into a hidden target-filesystem sibling followed by rename, and non-file/non-directory staged entries are rejected during cross-filesystem copy.

Model directory layout, installed-model discovery, broken metadata handling, active-model deletion guards, and human short-id display were audited earlier under ASR-MODEL-001/CLI-RESOURCE-001 and are not re-owned here. This unit therefore closes the remaining model-registry installation implementation without duplicating those decisions.

Deterministic evidence includes tar/tar.zst/tar.bz2 safety and extraction tests, checksum helper and mismatch tests, URL-fallback staging tests, single-root live model install, repeated replacement, missing-checksum install, metadata persistence, materialization rollback/cross-filesystem tests, and strict all-target vinpst-registry Clippy.

audits.title: Provider and adapter registry scripts and managed publication
notes: Frozen registry_scripts owns provider/adapter registry parsing, dotted resource-id to managed-path mapping, 120-second ordered script download, executable permission publication, managed-entry detection, and config materialization that preserves existing timeout/environment/extra values while adding newly declared registry environment keys.

Current ownership is intentionally split across the already-owned vinpst-registry script schema/materializer, the downloader/asset boundary, CLI registry/config orchestration, and GUI transactional script management. No still-pending current source file maps cleanly one-to-one to this frozen unit, so current_files is empty and those mixed owners remain supporting rather than being double-counted.

Fixed managed-entry detection to match frozen lexical path semantics. Existing command-provider and adapter args are now compared after filesystem-independent lexical normalization, so harmless `.`/`..` path spelling differences no longer make an otherwise managed script look user-defined. Integration tests now update both provider and adapter entries whose stored args contain a `./` segment.

Strengthened script publication around the frozen executable-permission boundary. A downloaded script is now staged into a unique same-directory prepared sibling, marked executable there, and only then renamed to the managed final path. If chmod fails, the prior managed script remains untouched and the prepared file is removed. A deterministic injected-permission failure test proves the old script survives with no prepared-file residue.

Fixed a CLI-only cross-resource consistency gap found while tracing frozen DownloadScript plus config materialization. Provider/adapter install now use a shared short transaction: preserve an existing managed script in a same-directory rollback sibling (or record that no script existed), install the new script, commit the validated config, then discard the rollback. Any install/post-check/config-write failure restores the previous script or removes a newly created script.

A process-level provider update test performs a real local HTTP script download, deliberately makes the config output path a directory so the config write fails after script publication, and proves the command fails while the prior managed script and input config are restored and no `.cli-rollback` file remains. Adapter installation uses the same shared transaction helper and its normal install suite remains green.

The CLI rollback helper rejects non-regular existing managed targets before update, copies and fsyncs an existing script before publication, restores with a same-directory rename, and treats rollback failure as additional error context. Cleanup of a rollback artifact after a fully successful script+config commit is best-effort so a valid committed state is not falsely reported as failed solely because an obsolete backup could not be deleted.

Current registry parsing remains deliberately stricter than frozen permissive item skipping: it validates positive version, duplicate ids/short ids, non-empty short ids/commands/URLs/env names, unique env keys, expected resource kind, and provider stream flag agreement with the `.streaming` id suffix. The current upstream public provider/adapter registries were inspected during this audit and conform to these constraints (11 providers and one adapter, all command `python3` entries with three script mirrors).

Frozen RelativePathForId behavior is preserved for multi-segment leaf ids. Frozen IdFromRelativePath has no production caller in the source tree and is not reproduced as an otherwise unused public Rust API. Managed roots preserve Vinpst identity rather than frozen Vinput paths.

Frozen readme_url, stream, script_urls, and env metadata all have current consumers: CLI available-resource output exposes readme/protocol/env requirements, GUI install preparation consumes environment declarations, and script installation uses ordered script_urls. No additional metadata field was found stranded by the rewrite.

Current GUI keeps its stronger persistent adapter rollback/revision and recovery state above the common script installer; the new atomic prepared-script publication composes with that layer rather than replacing it. GUI-only removal/revision policies remain owned by their later GUI audit units.

Deterministic evidence includes registry parser/materialization integration tests, ordered mirror download plus executable permission, lexical-equivalent managed provider/adapter update tests, injected chmod-failure preservation, the CLI config-write rollback process test, existing GUI script recovery/rollback tests, and strict all-target Clippy for registry/CLI/GUI.

audits.title: Configuration pointer routing and symlink-safe edit targets
notes: Frozen ConfigRouter maps core/Fcitx edit targets, implements JSON-pointer get/set over the core config, parses set values as JSON with string fallback, requires the destination pointer to already exist, and resolves symlink edit targets before modification.

Current JSON-pointer ownership already lives in CLI-CONFIG-001. It preserves the frozen parse rule (valid JSON becomes typed JSON; parse failure becomes a string) and existing-pointer requirement, while adding explicit --string, --stdin, --exists/default, dry-run, output, and in-place workflows. These extensions remain user-facing Vinpst improvements rather than aliases for test plumbing.

Current config set patches the loaded raw JSON document, validates the patched document through the typed schema, then persists the raw patched document. This retains unrelated forward-compatible JSON fields instead of forcing every pointer mutation through a complete typed reserialization; typed provider/adapter extra fields are also covered by CFG-CORE-001 preservation tests.

Fixed a real symlink regression shared by CLI and GUI writes. The Rust atomic writers previously staged a replacement beside the user-supplied path and renamed over that path, which replaced a final config symlink with a regular file. Frozen ResolveSymlinkPath/AtomicWriteTextFile instead writes through the symlink to its resolved target.

vinpst-config now exports one bounded resolve_symlink_write_target helper shared by typed persistence and CLI raw/private writers. It follows final symlink chains up to 32 levels, interprets relative targets relative to the link parent, and resolves a missing leaf through a symlinked parent without requiring the final file to exist. All temporary files are created beside the resolved target before rename.

Typed VinpstConfig persistence now resolves the actual destination before creating directories, staging the temporary config, copying backup contents, and renaming. The write receipt and requested backup path remain expressed in terms of the user-facing entry path, so a dotfiles symlink remains visible while its adjacent `.bak` still provides the familiar recovery location.

CLI write_file_atomically/write_private_file_atomically use the same resolver. This covers raw Fcitx config editing and every CLI JSON/config mutation that uses the shared writer, not just `config edit`. Resolved target parents are created before staging so a symlink can point at a not-yet-created target hierarchy.

Deterministic typed persistence proof creates a relative `config.json -> dotfiles/config.json` symlink, writes a validated update with backup, and proves the symlink identity/target text survive while the real file changes and the entry-path backup preserves the old contents.

Process-level CLI proofs cover both persistence families: `config set --in-place` through a relative core-config symlink preserves the link, updates the real JSON target, and writes the old target contents to `config.json.bak`; `config edit fcitx` through a relative Fcitx symlink preserves the link while an actual editor changes the real target and an adjacent backup records the prior text.

Frozen GetEditTarget treats every non-core string as Fcitx; current CLI accepts only the explicit public `core`/`fcitx` target enum, a deliberate input-validation improvement. Default paths retain Vinpst identity under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fcitx-vinpst` and Fcitx `vinpst.conf` rather than upstream Vinput names.

No current source file is newly claimed here: commands/config.rs, config_io.rs, and config persistence already have dedicated CLI-CONFIG/CLI-EDITOR/CFG-CORE owners, while paths.rs remains pending for the later path-utils audit. They are supporting files only, preserving non-overlapping ledger ownership.

Evidence includes existing JSON-pointer/string/stdin/missing-pointer/forward-field tests, new typed and process-level symlink preservation tests, strict all-target Clippy for vinpst-config and vinpst-cli, and the broader config/CLI suites run at closeout.

audits.title: Atomic text-file persistence and symlink-safe file utilities
notes: Frozen file_utils provides unrestricted whole-file text reads, parent-directory creation, symlink-target resolution, and mkstemp-based atomic text writes that flush the temporary file before rename. Callers include core config persistence, registry caches/i18n, context-history compaction, and model metadata publication.

Final symlink-target preservation was fixed and proven under CONFIG-ROUTER-001; this unit audits the remaining generic file semantics without re-owning vinpst-config persistence or CLI config_io. No unowned Rust source maps cleanly one-to-one to the frozen utility, so current_files remains empty.

Fixed the CLI ordinary atomic writer used by user-systemd service installation. The previous temporary name was only `<target>.tmp-<pid>` and used fs::write, so two writers in the same process could overwrite the same temporary file and race a rename. It now allocates a create_new temporary sibling with a bounded sequence, writes the complete body, fsyncs the file, then renames and removes any failed temporary.

The CLI private writer now reuses the same unique create_new naming discipline while retaining mode 0600, write_all, fsync, symlink-target resolution, and cleanup. Ordinary service-unit writes intentionally retain normal umask-derived permissions rather than forcing frozen mkstemp mode 0600 onto non-sensitive systemd unit files.

A deterministic two-thread CLI unit test releases concurrent ordinary writers onto one final path. Both writes must succeed, the final file must equal one complete payload rather than a torn mix, and no `.tmp-` sibling may remain. This specifically proves the old same-process temporary-name collision is closed.

Fixed RegistryTextCache durability to match frozen AtomicWriteTextFile more closely: cache publication now uses a create_new sibling, write_all plus fsync, rename, and cleanup. Existing fresh/stale cache semantics are unchanged. A two-thread registry test proves concurrent cache writers use distinct temporaries, leave a complete final body, and leave no `.tmp.` residue.

Fixed recent-input context-cache compaction, another frozen AtomicWriteTextFile caller. Truncation now writes through a unique create_new sibling, fsyncs before rename, and cleans failures instead of reusing a fixed `.tmp` path. New context-cache files and compaction temporaries use mode 0600 on Unix because the JSONL contains user input history.

Focused context tests prove both initial JSONL append and subsequent tail compaction preserve content semantics while resulting cache permissions are 0600 on Unix. Missing-cache truncation remains a no-op, and the five-second/100-write scheduling policy remains owned by the earlier Fcitx/context-history audit.

Frozen ReadTextFile itself has no maximum size; current size limits remain correctly owned by higher-level downloader/startup-notification/hotword boundaries instead of being forced into a generic file helper. Likewise frozen AtomicWriteTextFile fsyncs the temporary file but not the containing directory, so current paths that additionally sync directories retain their stronger durability policy.

Model metadata is written inside a private installation staging tree and the completed tree is then atomically materialized under REGISTRY-MODELS-001; it is intentionally not refactored into this text-file utility slice merely to centralize fs::write calls.

Evidence includes CONFIG-ROUTER symlink proofs, concurrent CLI and registry atomic-writer tests, registry fresh/stale/partial-temp tests, context JSONL append/truncate/permissions tests, and strict all-target Clippy for vinpst-text, vinpst-registry, and vinpst-cli.

audits.title: Canonical user paths, XDG roots, and managed resource locations
notes: Frozen path_utils centralizes XDG config/data/cache roots, core/Fcitx config locations, managed model/provider/adapter directories, registry/cache/runtime state, systemd service locations, Flatpak executable/template paths, and HOME-based tilde expansion. The Rust rewrite had equivalent successful-path values but several copies of the same XDG fallback policy across CLI, GUI, daemon, and Fcitx-FFI.

Added one small vinpst-config::user_paths module because CLI, GUI, daemon, ASR, and Fcitx-FFI already depend on vinpst-config. It owns only side-effect-free current-user product-path resolution: non-empty XDG overrides win, empty overrides fall back to non-empty HOME, and missing/empty XDG plus HOME returns None. This removes duplicated environment parsing without introducing another crate.

CLI paths.rs is now a thin user-facing error-context layer over the shared policy and is newly owned here. It retains CLI-only quote_exec_arg formatting, while config/data/model/provider/adapter/cache/staging/D-Bus activation/systemd locations come from the shared path owner. The stale generic HOME error that always mentioned XDG_DATA_HOME was replaced by path-specific diagnostics.

GUI config, model, model-staging, registry-cache, provider/adapter script, and startup-notification read-state paths now consume the same shared policy. Daemon default config and managed model roots and the Fcitx context-history config lookup do the same. These mixed files remain supporting rather than being double-owned.

Fixed a real XDG edge case in Silero VAD discovery: an explicitly present but empty XDG_DATA_HOME previously prevented the HOME/.local/share fallback. VAD now reuses user_paths::user_data_home while preserving the existing fcitx-vinpst/vad location and later XDG_DATA_DIRS/development fallbacks. The same shared empty-value semantics now apply to product config/data/cache paths everywhere.

The automatic registry local-i18n override intentionally remains under the legacy-compatible `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vinpst/i18n.local.json` namespace, but its XDG/HOME root selection now uses the shared policy so an empty XDG_CONFIG_HOME correctly falls back to HOME. The recent-input context cache likewise intentionally remains `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/vinpst/context.jsonl`; its domain helper and documented fallback-to-relative behavior are not migrated to the Vinpst product root.

Vinpst-owned persistent product state intentionally uses `fcitx-vinpst` rather than frozen `vinput`: config.json, models, providers, adapters, registry/model-install cache, and GUI read_notifications all preserve the project identity contract already documented for current users. Fcitx addon config remains `fcitx5/conf/vinpst.conf`.

Adapter runtime remains owned by vinpst-text and preserves the frozen XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -> TMPDIR -> /tmp ordering through non-empty XDG_RUNTIME_DIR plus std::env::temp_dir(), with only the product namespace changed to vinpst/adapters. Provider-script and text-adapter path expansion preserve HOME-relative `~` support; provider-script resolution deliberately rejects `~other-user/...` instead of reproducing frozen ExpandUserPath's accidental `$HOME/other-user/...` interpretation.

Frozen Flatpak paths under `/app/addons/Vinput`, executable names `vinput`/`vinput-daemon`, and service unit `vinput-daemon.service` are not reproduced. Current packaging uses Vinpst identities, direct typed daemon control, and its already-audited Flatpak/systemd layout. The shared path module therefore covers user-state roots only rather than reintroducing upstream package names.

Deterministic evidence includes pure XDG precedence/empty-value tests, CLI init/activation/systemd process tests, daemon discovered-XDG-config proof, Fcitx context-history tests, ASR VAD tests, and strict all-target Clippy across config/ASR/CLI/GUI/daemon/Fcitx-FFI. Closeout also searches the Rust tree to ensure remaining direct XDG_CONFIG/DATA/CACHE computations are only the shared helper, the intentional context-cache domain path, and a GUI test fixture.

audits.title: Process execution, monitored adapter supervision, and descendant cleanup
notes: Frozen process_utils exposes RunCommandWithInput, SpawnDetached, and SpawnForMonitoring. Its real call graph is narrow: RunCommandWithInput is used only by command-batch ASR and output ducking, SpawnForMonitoring only by the daemon text-adapter manager, and SpawnDetached has no production caller.

The shared vinpst-process crate already supersedes frozen RunCommandWithInput with an isolated Unix process group, one deadline covering stdin write/execution/output recovery, concurrent stdout/stderr draining, independent 1 MiB output caps, and bounded TERM-to-KILL cleanup of descendants. Command ASR, command text processing, and output-ducker helpers already use this boundary. These stronger fail-closed semantics are intentionally retained instead of reproducing direct-child-only SIGKILL and unbounded output.

Added a shared set_nonblocking(fd) helper to vinpst-process so long-lived supervisors can preserve descriptor flags while enabling O_NONBLOCK without duplicating fcntl policy. Specialized streaming ASR remains a domain supervisor because it has bidirectional frame/event semantics rather than one-shot command execution.

A real parity gap existed in long-lived text-adapter startup: current previously redirected adapter stderr to /dev/null, wrote the fingerprinted PID immediately, and only reaped adapters from status/runtime refresh calls. Frozen SpawnForMonitoring pipes nonblocking stderr, waits 250 ms before accepting startup, returns immediate-exit stderr as the start failure, and continuously emits each stderr line as a raw DaemonNotification.

Restored that behavior while preserving Rust safety improvements. Text adapters now start in the existing process group with stderr piped/nonblocking; a 250 ms startup probe runs before /proc fingerprint sampling and PID publication, so an immediate exit reports trimmed stderr (or a generic immediate-exit error) and leaves no PID file. If startup survives, the existing fingerprinted PID record is published exactly as before.

StartedAdapterProcess now drains available stderr without blocking, preserves partial lines across reads, trims ASCII whitespace, flushes a final partial line at EOF, and caps one pending line at the shared 1 MiB process-output bound with a truncation marker. Explicit StopAdapter intentionally does not flush stderr because frozen HandleStopRequest closes the monitored stderr fd before termination as well.

Daemon RuntimeState now retains adapter stderr notifications in a bounded 256-entry queue so status methods may reap/process stderr without consuming notifications before the signal path sees them. A 100 ms D-Bus pump drains that queue, logs the adapter id for diagnostics, and emits frozen-compatible raw ErrorInfo (code unknown, empty subject/detail, original stderr line as raw_message). The pump also reaps exited adapters and removes their PID files without requiring a status query.

The daemon adapter-process module is dedicated to this lifecycle and is owned here: it covers start/stop/reap plus config-reload reconciliation that stops changed adapters, prestarts replacements, and rolls back the prior running set on failure, including managed-script rollback revisions. Existing process-group and PID-identity protections remain stronger than frozen PID-only supervision.

Working-directory failures remain fail-closed through std::process::Command rather than reproducing frozen child-side chdir failure being ignored. SpawnDetached is not reintroduced because frozen has no caller and current callers that launch editors/openers/system tools have dedicated, separately audited lifecycle contracts.

Deterministic evidence covers existing process descendant/timeout/output-limit tests, all adapter-runtime lifecycle tests, immediate-exit stderr without PID publication, line/partial stderr draining, daemon notification queue preservation, feature-gated session-bus StartAdapter immediate-failure proof, live raw DaemonNotification proof, and delayed-exit reap behavior. Strict all-target/all-feature Clippy and full process/text/daemon gates close the unit.

audits.title: String formatting, ASCII trimming, UTF-8 context boundaries, and binary sizes
notes: Frozen string_utils is header-only and provides printf-style FmtStr, binary-threshold FormatSize, ASCII whitespace trimming, simple UTF-8 first/last codepoint decoding, the legacy cp>=0x2E80 CJK boundary predicate, and sentence-ending punctuation classification.

There is no dedicated Rust string-utility module to own: typed format!/Display replaces FmtStr at each domain boundary, ASCII trimming is local to payload/error parsing, and the context-history owner already contains the CJK/UTF-8/punctuation helpers because those rules only serve recent-input buffering. These existing owners remain supporting rather than being double-owned.

Recent-input buffering matches the frozen valid-UTF-8 behavior: non-CJK fragments gain one separating space, either-side cp>=0x2E80 suppresses that space, and ., !, ?, CJK 。！？, ellipsis, or newline flushes the buffer. Rust strings are valid UTF-8 by construction, so frozen FirstUtf8Codepoint/LastUtf8Codepoint behavior on malformed byte sequences is intentionally not reproduced.

ASCII trimming uses Rust ASCII-whitespace predicates or explicit space/tab/CR/LF sets at the relevant parser boundary. Frozen std::isspace on ASCII bytes additionally recognizes vertical-tab/form-feed; current error-info trimming uses is_ascii_whitespace and therefore covers the complete ASCII set, while payload trimming intentionally preserves its already-audited protocol subset.

Frozen FormatSize divides by powers of 1024 but labels values KB/MB/GB in CLI model tables and GUI resource/progress surfaces. Current model/resource presentation intentionally labels binary quantities KiB/MiB/GiB (or bytes), which is more accurate and already stable in user-facing tests; the misleading frozen suffixes are not restored.

No production change is required. Existing text context-cache tests pin the spacing/punctuation rules, model CLI tests exercise size presentation in the user surface, and GUI model/resource units have dedicated formatter tests.

audits.title: OpenAI-compatible URL joining and scene model discovery
notes: Frozen url_utils is a single header-only JoinPath helper that trims trailing slashes from a base URL and appends a caller-supplied absolute path. Its production call graph has only two uses: `/chat/completions` in post-processing and `/models` in the GUI provider/model scene controls.

The existing Rust chat URL builder already covers the first caller and is intentionally stronger: parsed URLs preserve query/fragment components, a complete chat-completions endpoint is not appended twice, empty bases are rejected, and malformed/non-URL test inputs retain the simple frozen trailing-slash join fallback. Existing text tests pin those semantics.

The second caller exposed a real GUI gap. Frozen SetupProviderModelCombos keeps the model combo editable while asynchronously loading `GET <provider base>/models`, sends an optional Bearer API key, uses a 10-second deadline, normalizes `data[].id` by trimming/deduplicating/sorting, and discards stale replies when the selected provider changes. Current Scene editing previously exposed only a provider picker plus free-form model text with no discovery path.

Added a vinpst-text OpenAI-compatible model-discovery boundary: `/models` URL construction, the shared provider trust environment, redirects disabled by the existing HTTP client policy, 10-second request timeout, bounded UTF-8 response body, optional Bearer authentication, stable secret-free typed errors, and sorted/deduplicated non-empty model ids. Errors never include request URLs, API keys, or response bodies.
