Scene editing now starts model discovery when an existing provider-backed scene opens or when the provider selection changes. A monotonically wrapping generation plus provider id rejects stale asynchronous responses. Network work runs through the existing plain blocking-task boundary, so reqwest::blocking never nests inside the GUI Tokio runtime.

The Rust UI intentionally keeps the existing model text input enabled while discovery is in progress or unavailable and presents discovered ids as a supplemental pick list. This is simpler and less blocking than frozen temporarily disabling the editable combo; choosing a suggestion only copies its id into the same text field. Failure is one short localized hint and never exposes transport plumbing.

Frozen stores a process-global cache keyed by `base_url + api_key`. Current intentionally does not copy that static secret-bearing cache: discovery is scoped to the active Scene editor and refetched on a later editor/provider transition. This avoids global credential-derived state while retaining the user-facing convenience and stale-response protection.

The frozen GUI helper files that own SetupProviderModelCombos are not claimed by this unit because they contain additional GUI responsibilities still pending separate file-level audit. Scene management, its view, i18n, the text crate root, and the already-owned OpenAI module are supporting files only, so their broader ownership remains accurate.

Deterministic evidence includes a real local HTTP GET `/models` test proving Bearer transmission plus model trimming/deduplication/sorting, URL query/fragment joining tests, GUI generation/provider stale-response tests, discovered-model selection state tests, strict text/GUI Clippy, and the full text and GUI suites.

audits.title: Debug logging controls and sensitive diagnostic boundaries
notes: Frozen debug_log is a header-only `VINPUT_DEBUG` gate. Any value beginning with 1/t/T/y/Y enables printf-style stderr logging under a fixed prefix. Production callers include recognized ASR text, LLM provider URLs and request bodies, adapter stderr, audio timing/state, ASR metadata, and Fcitx trigger/D-Bus diagnostics.

Current intentionally does not recreate a Vinpst boolean plaintext-dump switch. The daemon initializes tracing_subscriber with EnvFilter::from_default_env(), using the standard RUST_LOG control and tracing-subscriber’s ERROR default when the variable is absent or invalid. This permits targeted module/level filters instead of enabling every debug site at once.

The existing VINPST_DAEMON_TRACE_STARTUP switch is not equivalent to frozen VINPUT_DEBUG: it prints only fixed startup lifecycle markers and does not include argv, config values, filesystem paths, user text, URLs, credentials, or provider payloads. It is retained as a narrow bootstrap diagnostic for failures that happen around logger/service setup.

A log-privacy issue discovered while auditing this boundary was fixed: the adapter stderr monitor must emit each line as a frozen-compatible raw DaemonNotification, but current also duplicated the complete stderr line into tracing::warn and therefore potentially into the user journal when RUST_LOG enabled warnings. The journal event now records only adapter_id plus the fact that stderr was emitted; the protocol notification remains unchanged.

Other current tracing sites were reviewed for raw text/URL/body/API-key fields. Runtime/audio/output-ducker events are state, identifiers, timing, volume, status, or already-redacted typed errors. No current analogue of frozen post_processor debug dumping of ASR text, LLM request body, or full provider URL is introduced.

The safer divergence is deliberate: protocol/user-facing diagnostics remain separately redacted or explicitly raw where the frozen wire contract requires it, while persistent diagnostic logs do not become an opt-in plaintext transcript of recognition and LLM traffic.

Deterministic evidence includes the private-session-bus adapter stderr notification test (raw notification still arrives), the complete default daemon suite, strict daemon Clippy with D-Bus integration enabled, source/call-graph review of every frozen debug-log caller, and current tracing-field review.

Final GUI composition review found that App still derived Debug across its complete state even though child provider/adapter/install types had already been redacted. That composition root also carries arbitrary filter text and OperationState success/failure strings, so deriving Debug could reintroduce user/error text into diagnostics without crossing a child redaction boundary. App now has an explicitly non-exhaustive structural Debug that reports only locale/page, filter lengths, config/daemon/operation categories, safe counts, and editor/resource/operation presence booleans. A regression injects filter, operation, URL, API-key, and extra-body secret markers and proves none appear in App Debug.

audits.title: Flatpak sandbox detection, permissions, host commands, logs, and daemon service bootstrap
notes: Frozen sandbox utilities have five responsibilities and all remain accounted for: `/.flatpak-info` detection, `flatpak-spawn --host` wrapping, sandbox-aware journal filtering, three required Flatpak filesystem permissions, and rewriting the packaged daemon user-service unit so the daemon runs through the Fcitx Flatpak. Current keeps the same responsibilities in the CLI/service layer rather than recreating them in the thin Fcitx addon.

Host command and log behavior is aligned modulo the product rename: sandboxed systemctl commands are shell-free `flatpak-spawn --host ...`; sandbox logs use the host journal's Flatpak tag plus a Vinpst grep filter, while native logs target `vinpst-daemon.service`. Service rewriting targets `org.fcitx.Fcitx5`, preserves daemon arguments, rewrites the daemon path to `/app/addons/Vinpst/bin/vinpst-daemon`, and installs an INT-based stop command as frozen did.

The audit found a real permission-detection bug. Current had interpreted frozen's loose `pipewire` substring check as `[Context] sockets=pipewire` and required an exact `xdg-config/systemd` entry. Actual Flatpak metadata produced by the frozen/documented overrides is `filesystems=...;xdg-run/pipewire-0;xdg-config/systemd:create;...`, so correctly configured users were falsely reported as missing PipeWire and systemd access. The parser now checks the three real filesystem grants and accepts writable `:rw`/`:create` modes while rejecting `:ro` for paths Vinpst must write.

`vinpst doctor` now returns exact `remediation_commands` for whichever Flatpak grants are missing: `xdg-run/pipewire-0`, `xdg-config/systemd:create`, and `xdg-cache`, followed by `flatpak kill org.fcitx.Fcitx5`. This restores the actionable recovery path from frozen's Control-page warning while intentionally keeping installation-policy popups out of the standalone Rust GUI; unlike the frozen warning, the current remediation does not accidentally omit the cache permission that its own checker requires.

Frozen also performs a sandbox-only service copy from the Fcitx addon constructor, only when the destination unit does not already exist. Current deliberately keeps that host-filesystem side effect out of the thin C++ addon. The equivalent operation is the hidden maintenance command `vinpst daemon install-service`, which reads the packaged Flatpak template, atomically installs or refreshes the user unit, and performs host `daemon-reload`; the Flatpak installation guide now invokes that packaged CLI through the Fcitx Flatpak before enabling the host user service.

The Flatpak release smoke now executes packaged `daemon install-service --dry-run --json` and asserts both sandbox rewriting and the exact packaged daemon ExecStart, so the service-bootstrap replacement is checked as part of the extension artifact rather than existing only as an unreferenced helper. The user installation guide also distinguishes the Flatpak extension from native packages and no longer assumes extension binaries are present on the host PATH.

Evidence includes locally generated Flatpak 1.18 `/.flatpak-info` metadata for the three override forms, six sandbox unit tests, six Flatpak-filtered CLI protocol tests, strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy, shell syntax/ShellCheck for the release smoke, and the module-parity checker. Broader live Fcitx/PipeWire/systemd Flatpak desktop validation remains the separately documented release-environment boundary rather than a SANDBOX-001 code gap.

audits.title: Management GUI application shell, navigation, desktop actions, save boundary, and startup notifications
notes: Frozen main/mainwindow provide the management application's outer shell: initialize the Qt desktop application and translations, expose Control/Resources/LLM/Hotwords tabs, provide Open Config and Save Settings actions, refresh pages after config changes, restart the daemon after saving, and perform the startup notification check. Current accounts for those responsibilities with the standalone Iced binary, typed Page navigation, desktop actions, central config-save boundary, embedded i18n, and startup notification state machine.

The toolkit-specific startup environment is intentionally not copied literally. Frozen sets `QT_IM_MODULE=fcitx` and `XMODIFIERS=@im=fcitx` only when absent because it is a Qt application. Current is an Iced/winit application and leaves Wayland/X11 input-method selection to the desktop session instead of forcing Qt/XIM variables that do not describe its toolkit. Runtime `.qm` discovery is likewise replaced by the current embedded typed English and Simplified Chinese catalogs.

The audit found one real desktop-shell regression: current forced `Theme::TokyoNight` for every user while frozen opts into desktop settings and otherwise uses the system Qt palette. The explicit Iced theme was removed. The workspace already enables Iced 0.14 `linux-theme-detection`, so the default application theme follows the detected system Light/Dark mode and responds to system theme changes rather than imposing an unrelated fixed palette.

The four frozen tabs map to the same four current pages, with a sidebar instead of QTabWidget and a larger 960x640 default appropriate to the richer standalone management surface. Current Open Config is stronger in Flatpak: it invokes `xdg-open` directly on native systems and `flatpak-spawn --host xdg-open` in the Fcitx sandbox, without a shell. Current keeps the window open after a successful save instead of closing it; typed page-local save/reset state and unsaved-change guards make that deliberate rather than a missing frozen close call.

Frozen saves the complete settings document and synchronously restarts the daemon. Current persists the complete typed VinpstConfig and calls the frozen-compatible ReloadAsrBackend D-Bus method, whose daemon implementation reloads and validates the config file, reconciles text adapters, replaces the complete runtime config when safe, rebuilds configured text processing, reconciles remote text, and queues/warm-prepares the selected ASR backend; busy runtime application is deferred until idle. Therefore the legacy method name does not mean current only adopts ASR fields.

A save-failure consistency hole was found while tracing that replacement path. A D-Bus reload can fail after the daemon runtime has accepted the candidate config, for example when remote-text listener reconciliation cannot bind. The GUI previously restored only the old config file and then reported that the previous config was restored, potentially leaving disk and runtime divergent. After restoring the old document it now issues a second reload to reconcile daemon state too; if that rollback reload fails, the error explicitly says that disk restoration succeeded but daemon-state restoration failed. Deterministic tests cover both rollback-reload success and failure.

Startup notification behavior is equivalent at the application-shell level while intentionally hardened. Current checks the Vinpst repository feed with a five-second request boundary, locale fallback, monotonic read marker, acknowledge/details actions, and silent network failure; unlike frozen's unrestricted QNetworkReply parsing it also has the shared HTTP response cap, title/text caps, HTTPS-only details links, secret-free Debug output, symlink-safe bounded read state, and atomic 0600 persistence. The presentation is an in-app state/banner rather than a blocking QMessageBox, but acknowledgement and details still mark the notification read.

Evidence includes source-level call-graph review of all three frozen app-shell files, the complete current GUI suite, strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy, GUI help/version checks, focused config rollback-reconciliation tests, local inspection of Iced 0.14 system-theme behavior, and the module-parity checker. Page-specific Control/Resources/LLM/Hotwords implementations, i18n internals, and broader lib.rs orchestration remain separately pending and are not claimed by this unit.

audits.title: Text-adapter and ASR-provider editor presentation contracts
notes: Frozen adapter_dialog is a thin command-adapter editor: immutable id, command, one-argument-per-line args, and KEY=VALUE environment lines. Current preserves the same edit identity and process fields, adds an optional working directory, and routes them through a typed editor that trims command/path boundaries, preserves forward-compatible adapter metadata, rejects stale concurrent edits, validates the complete resulting config, and keeps process configuration out of Debug output.

Current intentionally keeps args as a JSON string array instead of frozen's trimmed non-empty line syntax. This is less visually terse but losslessly represents whitespace and arbitrary argument strings without inventing shell parsing. The audit did find that the entire args field had been rendered as a password field even though arguments are ordinary user-visible process configuration in frozen and usually need inspection while editing. Adapter and command-ASR args are now visible in the form; environment values and credential-bearing endpoints remain masked/redacted.

Frozen asr_provider_dialog can represent local or command providers, locks id/type while editing, exposes timeout/model/command/args/env, and gives local providers an editable combo populated from installed model directories. Current retains immutable edit identity/type, supports the same local and command fields plus an additive remote-provider type and structured environment rows, and preserves model semantics for command/remote providers because current runtimes actually consume the optional model id there.

A real local-provider usability regression was fixed. Current had reduced the frozen editable installed-model combo to a bare model text field even though the standalone GUI already maintains a typed scan of installed models. Local ASR forms now keep manual model entry while also listing usable installed model ids with a Use action; selection writes InstalledModelInfo::config_model_value(), the same concrete model directory consumed by the existing Resources model-selection path. Broken model installations are excluded rather than suggested as runnable backends.

Frozen's nominal 15000 ms constructor default is not copied into current new-provider state. Source call-graph review shows the frozen dialog is invoked from ControlPage's edit path, while local providers are not editable there; configured provider timeout values are therefore the meaningful compatibility contract. Current blank timeout deliberately means backend default and validates any explicit value as a positive integer, avoiding a new hard-coded timeout policy for the additive custom-provider flow.

The frozen dialogs defer parsing helpers and persistence/reload to their page call sites. Current likewise keeps view ownership narrow: broader add/edit/remove persistence, daemon reconciliation, managed-script policy, model registry scanning, and page orchestration remain supporting pending files for their later dedicated audits rather than being claimed here. Current additionally prevents dirty editor state from being silently discarded by conflicting page/resource operations.

Evidence includes full source and call-site review of all four frozen dialog files, source review of frozen NonEmptyLines/ParseCommandEnv behavior, current typed editor/persistence paths, installed-model config value semantics, focused 8-test ASR-provider and 10-test adapter-editor suites, strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy, and the module-parity checker.

audits.title: Control page audio, daemon lifecycle, and live ASR state
notes: Frozen ControlPage owns capture-device selection, normalize/input-gain/output-duck/VAD settings, configured ASR provider actions, daemon Start/Stop/Restart, two-second daemon refresh, live ASR target/effective markers, and a Flatpak permission warning. Current Control preserves the audio fields through a typed config draft, asynchronous PipeWire discovery, atomic config-save boundary, typed daemon controls, and provider/resource management. The Flatpak permission warning and remediation path were already audited and fixed by SANDBOX-001 and are intentionally not double-owned here.

The audit found a real live-state regression. Current previously labeled the configured active_provider as Active without consulting the daemon's frozen-compatible eight-field GetAsrBackendState, so a newly saved provider could appear active while it was still loading or after reload failure left the previous backend effective. DaemonSnapshot now carries optional boxed AsrBackendState, Control provider rows distinguish configured/effective/loading/reload-failed state, and the Control page refreshes that state every two seconds through the existing non-activating owner poll rather than accidentally D-Bus-activating a stopped service.

Current endpoint semantics differ subtly from frozen. Frozen reports remote_text_service ListEndpoints, while current daemon diagnostics attach the configured target remote endpoints. To avoid showing a failed target endpoint beside a still-effective previous backend, the GUI only renders remote endpoints after target provider/model and effective provider/model converge. Focused projection tests cover same-provider model loading, successful convergence, failed replacement with previous-backend fallback, and endpoint suppression.

Frozen also appends loading backend or backend error to the daemon status label. Current now restores those generic indicators from AsrBackendState while deliberately never surfacing raw last_error there. DaemonSnapshot has a custom redacted Debug implementation: target/effective ids and state booleans remain diagnosable, but raw backend errors and endpoint strings are replaced by presence/count metadata. A Message::DaemonLoaded regression test verifies credential-like error text and endpoint tokens cannot leak through Debug.

Audio controls are equivalent at the frozen boundary: current enumerates PipeWire sources, always offers default, exposes normalize audio, 0.1-10.0 input gain, output ducking with 0-100 percent volume, and VAD enablement. Current additionally exposes VAD threshold and preserves a configured capture-device id that temporarily disappears from enumeration instead of silently replacing it with default; both are intentional standalone-GUI improvements. Discovery failure is explicit and retryable rather than collapsing the selector silently.

Frozen treats its built-in local provider as a special non-editable/non-removable Control row. Current intentionally does not copy that special case: Local, Remote, and Command are first-class AsrProviderConfig entries with stable ids, local model/hotword fields, and the previously audited local installed-model editing flow. Active providers remain protected from removal, registry-managed providers use managed removal, and all mutations go through complete config validation and daemon reconciliation.

Daemon lifecycle parity is preserved and hardened. Start activates through the D-Bus service, while Stop/Restart use the typed systemd user-service command path; after service actions current performs a non-activating owner/runtime observation and reports confirmed, contradictory, or unavailable final state instead of assuming systemctl success means the requested runtime state was reached. Stale asynchronous completions cannot overwrite a newer daemon-control operation.

Evidence includes complete source review of frozen control_page.cpp/.h and current audio_devices.rs, config_editor.rs, and daemon_control.rs; supporting review of ASR provider/config schema and D-Bus snapshot paths; focused live-state and Debug-redaction regressions; strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy; full GUI tests; and the module-parity ledger checker. Shared daemon_client/resource_pages/lib/i18n/message orchestration and broader ASR-provider persistence remain pending for later ownership-specific audits.

audits.title: Hotword page path, content, and provider-aware editing flow
notes: Frozen HotwordPage is a thin single-file editor: it finds the first local ASR provider, shows its hotwordsFile path, loads that file into a text editor on page reload or after Browse/path editing, documents the optional `word 2.0` score syntax, and exposes path/content accessors to MainWindow. Current retains all user-facing capabilities and the score syntax in both English and Simplified Chinese, while making the page provider-aware for every hotword-capable Local or Command provider instead of implicitly binding the UI to the first Local entry.

The apparent auto-load difference is intentional rather than a missing compatibility feature. Frozen MainWindow's global Save reads HotwordPage::hotwordsContent and directly truncates/writes the selected file before saving config; automatic page/file loading is therefore necessary to avoid a normal settings save erasing an untouched hotword file. Current removes that unsafe coupling: Browse changes only the path draft, Set/Clear Path are explicit config transactions, Load Content creates a file snapshot, Save Content is a separate conflict-aware publication, and ordinary settings saves do not rewrite hotword files. Reintroducing implicit load/write coupling would weaken current's transactional boundary rather than improve parity.

Frozen applies one HotwordPage path to every Local provider during MainWindow save even though page reload reads only the first Local provider. Current instead selects a concrete hotword-capable provider, preserves that selection across config refresh when still valid, prefers the active provider when possible, and mutates only the selected provider. Remote providers are excluded; Command providers are supported because current schema/runtime explicitly permit hotwords_file there.

Current Browse uses the native/portal-backed file chooser with the same text/all-files intent, starts from the current file or parent directory when valid, treats cancel as a no-op, and keeps selected paths and chooser errors out of Debug output. A picked path invalidates stale loaded content but is not silently persisted, so the user cannot accidentally retarget a provider merely by inspecting another file.

Current content editing deliberately requires an explicit loaded baseline. Provider/path changes are blocked while content is dirty; stale asynchronous loads are rejected if provider or resolved path changed; Reset restores the last loaded snapshot; and saved-but-not-applied hotword changes retain a retryable activation state. These are additive safety semantics over frozen's unguarded QFile read/write flow and preserve the same editable raw one-entry-per-line file format.

Path semantics are also stricter by design. Current trims configured values, rejects URL-like hotword paths, refuses ambiguous cross-process relative paths where daemon and GUI resolution could differ, validates the complete resulting config before persistence, and distinguishes configured path from the resolved content path. Those resolution and durability primitives remain supporting pending modules for their own file-level audits; this unit owns the page state machine, chooser, and presentation rather than claiming every filesystem primitive underneath them.

Evidence includes complete source and MainWindow call-site review of frozen hotword_page.cpp/.h, complete review of current hotword_management.rs plus its view/file-picker modules and page tests, the full 212/212 GUI library suite plus 1/1 main test, and the module-parity checker. No production-code change was required for this unit.

audits.title: LLM providers, adapters, scenes, and runtime controls
notes: Frozen LlmPage combines four user flows: OpenAI-compatible provider CRUD/Test, configured adapter runtime management, Scene CRUD/activation, and a pointer to registry-managed adapter installation on Resources. Current preserves all four flows while separating durable configuration, daemon-authoritative runtime state, registry installation, and page presentation instead of treating the page widget as the persistence boundary.

Provider CRUD parity is preserved and hardened. Current keeps provider ids immutable during edit, validates and atomically persists the complete config, clears removed provider references from Scenes like frozen, preserves forward-compatible extra fields, masks sensitive URL components, and keeps API keys/extra_body out of Debug. Frozen Test probes GET /models; current intentionally tests the production /chat/completions path with a provider default model or an unambiguous Scene model. The frozen-compatible /models discovery capability is still available in the Scene editor and was audited by URL-UTILS-001, so the production-path Test remains an intentional product divergence rather than a missing capability.

Adapter configuration and runtime are complete. Custom command adapters support id/command/args/environment/working-directory editing with stable identities and full-config validation, while managed adapters follow the registry removal path. Runtime Start/Stop uses daemon-authoritative TextAdapterState with precondition refresh, postcondition confirmation, stale-generation guards, and explicit contradictory/unavailable outcomes instead of assuming a D-Bus call means the process reached the requested state. Current deliberately rejects frozen's adapter tooltip behavior that exposes full argv and environment values; ordinary args remain visible in the editor but environment input and Debug are redacted.

The audit found two real Scene-editor compatibility regressions. Frozen LlmPage deliberately overrides the frozen core/CLI candidate default of 1 and starts newly added GUI Scenes at 3; current GUI had inherited 1. SceneEditorState::add now restores the page-specific default of 3 without changing the CLI/core default. Frozen also permits an empty Label and displays the Scene id as fallback, while current strict schema requires a non-empty label; the GUI now mirrors the already-audited CLI compatibility rule by normalizing a blank label to the stable Scene id before validation.

Current intentionally does not copy frozen's QSpinBox-only 1..10 candidate restriction. The current typed configuration contract accepts candidate_count through 0..32 and validates the complete Scene against that schema; narrowing only the GUI would make valid current configs uneditable and would also copy a frozen inconsistency, because its postprocess core separately normalizes 0..9. The GUI keeps the current 0..32 contract while restoring only the frozen page-specific default. Blank timeout remains serialized as None but the runtime effective default is the frozen 4000 ms, an intentional representation difference already covered by prior config/CLI audits.

Scene provider/model selection remains stronger than frozen without losing its affordances. Current lists configured providers, retains free-form model entry, asynchronously discovers /models suggestions with Bearer auth, timeout/size bounds and stale-generation rejection, protects built-in Scenes from destructive removal, rejects stale edits, and reconciles daemon state after mutation. Activate/remove operations are explicit and cannot overwrite an unrelated unsaved config draft.

The audit also restored the frozen navigation hint for adapters. The LLM page now tells users in English and Simplified Chinese to install managed adapters from Resources and return to LLM for Start/Stop, while retaining Add Custom Adapter for local manual configuration. This points at the existing registry catalog rather than duplicating installation controls on two pages.

Evidence includes complete source review of frozen llm_page.cpp/.h; complete review of current provider, adapter-config, adapter-runtime, Scene management and their dedicated views; supporting review of Resources registry installation and current config validation; 17 provider tests, 9 adapter-config tests, 6 adapter-runtime tests, 11 Scene tests, localization completeness tests, strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy, the full GUI suite, and the module-parity ledger checker. Shared resource_pages/i18n/script catalog/install orchestration stays pending for later ownership-specific audits.

Final composition-root localization review found one adapter-editor conflict guard still authored as a hard-coded English sentence. The English wording is preserved exactly, while the guard now routes through GuiLocale with a zh_CN form so cross-page/runtime/resource blocking remains consistent with the rest of the typed adapter UI.

audits.title: Resource catalogs, managed installs, selection, and removal
notes: Frozen ResourcePage combines installed-model management with live model/provider/adapter registries, four independent search boxes, asynchronous downloads, progress/log presentation, model activation/removal, and provider/adapter script installation. Current preserves those resource lifecycles while using typed operation state, shared registry/cache helpers, detail panels, cancellation, generation guards, and explicit recovery instead of widget-owned workers and a free-form log box.

The audit found a real discoverability regression in filtering. Current previously applied its only Resources filter solely to available registry models, so installed models and provider/adapter catalogs could not be searched at all. Resources now exposes one intentionally simpler global filter at the top of the page rather than copying four separate frozen boxes. The same query filters installed managed models, available model entries, ASR-provider registry entries, and LLM-adapter registry entries using stable ids, short ids, localized/fallback titles, descriptions, model directory names, backend/language/runtime/family metadata as applicable. Empty filtered results are distinguished from genuinely empty catalogs with explicit localized match text.

Managed-model installation is stronger than frozen's page-owned DownloadWorker. Current resolves localized live registry metadata, uses cancellable controlled downloads with progress snapshots and operation generations, verifies and publishes through the registry installer, rescans installed metadata after completion, and exposes retry/cancel state. Stale worker completions cannot replace a newer install state. Frozen's detailed transfer-speed/log text is intentionally represented by typed phase/progress UI rather than retained as a compatibility requirement.

Using an installed model targets only the configured active Local ASR provider, rejects Remote/Command targets, validates the complete cloned config, atomically persists through the audited save/reload boundary, reloads the GUI document after success, and refreshes daemon state. This preserves frozen's Use semantics while avoiding its special preferred-local side channel. Unsaved Control drafts and open Scene/ASR-provider editors block the mutation rather than being overwritten.

Removal is conservative. Current requires an explicit confirmation dialog and passes every Local provider model path to managed-model removal, so a model referenced by any configured local provider cannot be deleted even if that provider is inactive; frozen only had to reason about its single preferred local model. Managed ASR providers cannot be removed while active, managed adapter/provider cleanup validates and saves config before deleting the published script, and custom entries are routed through their validated configuration removal paths.

Provider/adapter Install and Update avoid frozen's half-installed blind spot. Preparation first refetches/resolves the selected registry entry, materializes and validates the prospective config, and collects registry-declared environment values with required-value enforcement and redacted Debug. Installation is cancellable, prepares rollback state before publication, verifies the installed path, applies managed-script revision metadata, then commits configuration through daemon reconciliation. Publication/config failure becomes a distinct RecoveryRequired state that can retry only configuration recovery without downloading or publishing the script again; stale preparation/install/recovery completions are rejected by operation id.

Registry refresh semantics intentionally differ in presentation. Frozen Refresh updates all three resource registries together and reloads i18n; current primes all catalogs during GUI boot and provides separate refresh controls for model, provider, and adapter catalogs, each with localized cache-aware mirror fallback. A single failed catalog therefore no longer prevents the other resource classes from remaining usable. This is an additive availability improvement, not a missing Refresh capability.

Evidence includes complete source review of frozen resource_page.cpp/.h and current model_install.rs, model_management.rs, model_selection.rs, removal_confirmation.rs, resource_pages.rs, script_catalog.rs, script_install.rs, and script_install/view.rs; transaction-contract review of script_management publication/save/rollback paths; focused Resources, model-management, script-install, removal, selection and i18n tests; strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy; the full GUI suite; and the module-parity ledger checker. Shared low-level script transaction/recovery/removal primitives and current-only resource detail panels remain pending for their own ownership-specific audits.

Follow-up current-only script-transaction review found one remaining registry URL construction bypass in the GUI model catalog: it still appended `/registry/models.json` by string concatenation, so a valid mirror URL carrying query/fragment data could place the catalog path inside the query instead of the URL path. model_management now reuses vinpst_registry::resolve_registry_url, with a regression covering parsed query/fragment mirrors and opaque mirror strings. This is the same path-before-query/fragment contract already fixed at the shared registry planning boundary.

audits.title: GUI configuration load, save, serialization, and change propagation
notes: Frozen ConfigManager is only a process-global Qt singleton around LoadCoreConfig/SaveCoreConfig: both calls are serialized with one QMutex, and a successful Save emits configChanged so pages reload the shared document. Current intentionally has no one-to-one singleton source file. The equivalent responsibilities are split between the typed vinpst-config persistence layer and the Rust GUI application's owned ConfigDocument state, so this upstream pair has no unique current file to claim.

Loading intentionally follows the already-established current config contract rather than frozen's permissive recovery semantics. The GUI resolves the canonical XDG user config path, loads and validates an existing typed document, and falls back to the bundled upstream-compatible default only when the user file is absent. A malformed, semantically invalid, or unsupported future config fails closed instead of being partially defaulted and later overwritten; this policy was already audited at the config-contract boundary and is preserved here.

Saving is materially stronger than the frozen mutex wrapper. Before a GUI mutation is persisted, current compares the on-disk document with the ConfigDocument snapshot and rejects external changes instead of silently winning a last-writer race. The candidate config is fully validated, serialized to a private temporary file beside the destination, synchronized, optionally backs up the existing target to the legacy-compatible `.bak` path, and is atomically renamed over the destination. Relative symlink targets are resolved deliberately and existing recovery backups are not destroyed merely because staging failed.

The frozen QMutex is therefore not copied as the primary concurrency primitive. Iced owns application-state mutation on its update loop, in-flight configuration mutations make conflicting GUI edit/navigation messages non-actionable, and filesystem conflict detection protects against other processes or independent writers. Worker completion paths reload the saved document before exposing success. This covers both intra-GUI serialization and cross-process races more precisely than one mutex that only protected callers sharing the same frozen singleton.

The frozen configChanged signal is replaced by explicit state reconciliation. A successful Control save calls replace_config(load_config_document(...)), which rebuilds the editable draft, reconciles hotword state, closes stale resource editors, and then refreshes daemon state. Scene/provider/adapter/hotword/script/model mutation completion paths likewise reload or replace the ConfigDocument after successful persistence, so all page views consume the new authoritative App state without a separate observer singleton. Failure leaves the prior in-memory document intact or presents the reload failure explicitly rather than emitting a misleading change notification.

Current additionally couples persistence to daemon reconciliation. Normal validated mutations request the daemon to reload the complete config; if the reload fails after disk commit, the previous disk document is restored and a second daemon reload attempts to restore runtime state as well. If runtime rollback also fails, the GUI reports that partial recovery explicitly. This daemon/disk two-phase recovery was audited under GUI-APP-SHELL-001 and is supporting evidence here, not newly owned functionality.

Evidence includes complete source review of frozen config_manager.cpp/.h; review of current default-path, typed-load, atomic persistence, external-change detection, replace_config propagation, save completion, and daemon rollback paths; 29 focused GUI `config_` tests, all 5 vinpst-config persistence tests, committed-default/bundled-default equivalence and validation tests, and the module-parity ledger checker. No production-code change is required for this unit.

audits.title: GUI blocking workers, progress delivery, and cooperative cancellation
notes: Frozen DownloadWorker is a generic QThread wrapper around one bool-returning closure plus error text. It also throttles progress emissions: duplicate percentages below 100 are suppressed and changed percentages are emitted at most every 100 ms. Current intentionally splits those responsibilities instead of preserving a GUI-specific arbitrary-task worker class.

blocking_task.rs owns the thread-execution boundary. Blocking reqwest/zbus and registry work runs on a named plain std thread rather than inside Tokio spawn_blocking, then returns through a typed oneshot into an Iced Task. Spawn failure and premature worker termination, including panic before result delivery, are explicit BlockingTaskFailure values. Operation closures and results are owned, so UI state is not borrowed across the worker lifetime.

vinpst-registry operation.rs owns long-operation control. RegistryOperationProgress is typed by phase and carries byte/entry counters where meaningful; RegistryOperationControl uses an Arc<AtomicBool> for cooperative cancellation, suppresses progress after cancellation, exposes check_cancelled to inner download/extract/publish loops, and deliberately redacts the reporter closure from Debug. This is stronger than frozen DownloadWorker, which has no cancellation API at all and whose destructor simply waits for the worker to finish.

Current preserves frozen's effective 10 Hz GUI progress cadence without embedding throttling inside the registry core. Model and script install workers update one shared latest typed progress value as often as needed; the Iced subscription samples that value every 100 ms. This avoids dispatching unbounded per-chunk UI messages while allowing inner operations to retain exact progress and cancellation checkpoints. Frozen's free-form transfer-speed string is intentionally replaced by typed byte/phase progress, as already documented by GUI-RESOURCE-PAGE-001.

Worker lifetime is intentionally non-blocking at GUI-state destruction. Active model installs, script preparation, and script installs call RegistryOperationControl::cancel from Drop; explicit Cancel does the same and marks the view cancelling. The underlying blocking thread is not synchronously joined merely because its UI state disappears, avoiding frozen's shutdown-time QThread::wait stall. The controlled registry loops own their inputs and observe cooperative cancellation before further publication work, while stale operation generations prevent late completions from mutating newer GUI state.

Evidence includes complete source review of frozen download_worker.cpp/.h and current blocking_task.rs/registry operation.rs; inspection of model/script worker Drop and explicit cancellation paths plus 100 ms progress subscriptions; the registry operation cancellation test, both blocking_task runtime-boundary tests, exact model drop/cancel tests, the script drop-cancellation test, and strict all-target Clippy for vinpst-registry and vinpst-gui. No production-code change was required.

audits.title: GUI helper validation, parsing, translation, and model suggestions
notes: Frozen gui_helpers is a mixed Qt utility bag: MainWindow-context translation, trimmed non-empty line splitting, read-only QTableWidget cells with UserRole data, LLM provider name/base-URL validation, KEY=VALUE command-environment parsing, and asynchronous provider /models suggestions for editable provider/model combos. Current intentionally distributes those responsibilities across typed editors and declarative views rather than preserving a generic GUI helper module, so there is no unique current file to claim.

The audit found one real compatibility gap in LLM-provider validation. Frozen ValidateProviderInput rejects invalid URLs, non-http(s) schemes, and URLs without a host before the provider can be saved. Current LlmProviderEditorState previously checked only that base_url was non-empty, and the typed config schema intentionally permits opaque non-empty base_url strings for forward compatibility; the GUI could therefore persist ftp://, file://, or relative provider targets and fail only when a request was attempted. The editor now parses the value and accepts only http or https URLs with a host, preserving localhost/explicit ports while rejecting unsupported or relative targets.

Provider URL validation errors are deliberately secret-free. The new guard returns one generic message and never interpolates the submitted URL, so credentials embedded in malformed or unsupported URLs cannot leak through an error dialog or Debug path. A regression uses a credential-bearing ftp URL and verifies the secret is absent from the error text. The broader base-URL masking logic for userinfo/query/fragment remains intact.

Frozen NonEmptyLines and ParseCommandEnvText are intentionally not copied literally. Current command/adapter argument editors use JSON string arrays and environment editors use JSON string objects, producing unambiguous typed values; environment values naturally retain arbitrary '=' characters instead of depending on first-equals line splitting. Current redaction is also stronger: frozen's invalid KEY=VALUE diagnostic embeds the complete offending line and may expose a secret value, whereas current parse errors describe the JSON contract without echoing environment contents.

Frozen MakeCell exists only to construct non-editable QTableWidgetItems and stash an optional identifier in Qt::UserRole. Iced resource/provider/adapter views are declarative: displayed text is immutable presentation data and row actions carry typed ids in Message values, so there is no mutable table-cell helper or hidden UserRole state to reproduce.

GuiTranslate maps non-QObject callers into the frozen MainWindow translation context. Current uses the typed GuiLocale/GuiText catalog throughout the application rather than dynamic QObject context lookup; the translation catalog itself remains pending for I18N-CACHE-001 and is only supporting evidence here.

Frozen PopulateProviderModelCombosAsync performs editable /models discovery with Bearer authorization and generation rejection. That capability was already audited and fixed by URL-UTILS-001: current Scene editing retains free-form model input plus provider-specific suggestions, stale-generation protection, a 10-second request boundary, 1 MiB response cap, Bearer support, and secret-free errors without frozen's global API-key cache. It is therefore referenced here rather than double-owned.

Evidence includes complete source and call-site review of frozen gui_helpers.cpp/.h; review of current LLM/ASR/adapter typed editor parsing, declarative resource views, localization boundary, and previously audited /models discovery; the exact provider URL regression, all 18 LLM-provider tests, all 9 adapter-config tests, strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: GUI static localization and dynamic registry i18n refresh
notes: Frozen I18nCache is specifically a process-global cache for registry-provided dynamic title/description strings. ReloadSync reads the merged registry i18n map under a mutex; ReloadAsync computes a fresh map off-thread and uses a generation counter so an older completion cannot overwrite a newer reload. GetMap returns a copy for page rendering. Current intentionally has no global mutable registry-i18n singleton: each model/provider/adapter catalog refresh resolves the current registry source plus locale-specific cached i18n into immutable display summaries, so stale page state is controlled by the existing catalog task/state boundary rather than a second shared cache generation.

The audit found a real locale-coupling regression. Current GUI static presentation intentionally supports only English and Simplified Chinese, but model/script registry localization incorrectly reused that GuiLocale to choose dynamic registry i18n. On a system such as fr_FR, GuiLocale correctly fell back to English for untranslated application chrome, but registry entries that did provide fr_FR translations were also forced to en_US. Frozen I18nCache independently calls DetectPreferredLocale and therefore still uses the French registry layer. Current model and script catalog loaders now independently call detect_preferred_registry_locale and pass that normalized locale through the registry-i18n fetch path, while GuiLocale remains responsible only for static application text.

The registry locale fix preserves frozen fallback precedence without expanding the static GUI language set. Dynamic catalog lookup fetches preferred locale plus en_US fallback through the already-audited 20-second/1-MiB cache-aware registry source and merges fallback before preferred. A deterministic fr_FR regression proves a French title and an English-only description coexist in the merged map. Existing zh_CN catalog tests remain unchanged.

Installed managed-model titles now follow the same separation. Installation metadata is already populated using the detected registry locale; Resources display and filtering now try that preferred registry locale first and the static GuiLocale code second, so a model installed under fr_FR does not regress to its English fallback merely because the application chrome has no French catalog.

Current static GUI localization is intentionally typed rather than QObject-context based. GuiText enumerates the complete user-facing key set, en.rs and zh_cn.rs provide exhaustive non-empty mappings, and GuiLocale detects LANGUAGE/LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES/LANG with legacy normalization before choosing zh_CN or the English fallback. Dynamic formatted/error strings stay in typed helper methods so machine ids, paths, and secret-redaction boundaries remain explicit. The localization completeness test iterates every GuiText key for both locales and prevents an added UI key from silently missing one language.

Registry-i18n parsing, arbitrary-locale normalization, mirror independence, local override precedence, stale disk cache behavior, and fetch orchestration were already fixed and owned by REGISTRY-I18N-001/REGISTRY-CACHE-001/REGISTRY-LIVE-FETCH-001. This unit therefore audits the GUI consumption/cache boundary and static catalog ownership without double-owning those registry primitives.

Evidence includes complete frozen i18n_cache.cpp/.h review; current GuiLocale architecture, exhaustive key/catalog mappings and localization tests; dynamic model/script catalog and installed-model lookup paths; the new arbitrary-locale merge regression, 2 script-catalog tests, 10 model-management tests, 6 i18n-focused tests, strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only configuration facade, typed errors, and diagnostic redaction
notes: This is a current-only ownership unit. The frozen project did not have a Rust crate facade or one typed ConfigError surface: those responsibilities arise from Vinpst splitting configuration into a reusable crate shared by CLI, daemon, and GUI. The already-audited schema/default/normalization/persistence behavior is not re-owned here; this unit covers only the public re-export boundary, structured error payloads, and shared diagnostic URL redaction helper left pending after the functional config audits.

diagnostics.rs defines the shared URL disclosure boundary used by ASR/text diagnostics. It parses without mutating the configured request URL, removes userinfo and fragments, preserves scheme/host/port/path and explicit-path shape, preserves query-key order and duplicates while replacing every query value with REDACTED, and maps malformed input to the fixed <invalid-url> marker. Its focused tests cover credentials, query values, duplicate query keys, path-shape preservation, and malformed input; config-contract.md documents the same contract.

The audit found one real secret-retention bug in ConfigError. DuplicateRegistryBaseUrl previously stored and displayed the literal duplicate mirror string. Because registry mirrors are not restricted to credential-free URLs and validation errors flow directly into GUI strings, CLI anyhow chains, and daemon RuntimeError, a mirror containing userinfo or query credentials could survive in both Display and derived Debug. Validation now stores redact_url_for_diagnostics(base_url) in this error variant instead. The error remains actionable by showing the sanitized mirror shape, while neither the typed error object nor downstream formatting retains the submitted credentials.

A deterministic regression duplicates a mirror containing username, password, query token, and fragment, then verifies both Display and Debug contain only https://example.test/v1?token=REDACTED and none of the four secret values. The existing duplicate-mirror test and legacy compatibility test remain green, demonstrating that ordinary credential-free mirrors keep the same typed error behavior while only sensitive components are removed.

The rest of ConfigError was reviewed variant by variant. JSON/read failures carry parser metadata or a filesystem path; validation variants carry ids, environment variable names, numeric limits, or empty-field markers rather than API keys, environment values, command arguments, extra bodies, or provider endpoints. InvalidRegistryBaseUrl retains the raw rejected string internally, but that branch is reachable only for trim-empty input and its Display is fixed, so it cannot retain a non-whitespace URL secret. No second secret-bearing error payload was found.

lib.rs intentionally exposes the typed schema, ConfigError, redaction helper, atomic persistence receipts/errors, and user-path module while keeping normalization/validation implementation modules private behind VinpstConfig methods. Its crate-level documentation was updated from migration-era 'first implementation' wording to the current shared configuration contract so v0.1.0 Rustdoc no longer describes completed migration work as future work.

Evidence includes complete source review of diagnostics.rs, error.rs, and lib.rs; call-chain inspection proving validation errors reach GUI, CLI, and daemon user-visible error surfaces; the new credential-bearing duplicate-mirror Display/Debug regression, existing redaction and legacy compatibility tests, the full vinpst-config all-target suite, strict all-target Clippy, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only protocol facade and sanitized text-adapter diagnostics
notes: This is a current-only protocol unit. recognition.rs is already owned by ASR-RESULT-001, while asr.rs, dbus.rs, and status.rs are owned by DBUS-PROTOCOL-001; lib.rs is therefore audited here only as the crate-level re-export boundary, and text.rs owns Vinpst's additional text-adapter diagnostic JSON that has no frozen one-to-one source file.

TextAdapterSummary deliberately carries only stable adapter id, implementation kind, argument/environment entry counts, running state, supervised pid, and a has-working-directory flag. The daemon producer computes these values from LlmAdapterConfig without copying command text, argument values, environment keys or values, or the working-directory path. Serialization and generated JSON schema tests both prove those detail fields are absent from the public summary shape.

TextAdapterState redundantly carries adapter_count, adapter_ids, single_adapter_id, and the summary list for existing CLI/D-Bus diagnostics. Outbound daemon state is built through from_adapters, which derives the count and ids from the same sanitized vector and only sets single_adapter_id when exactly one entry exists. The redundant fields are intentionally retained instead of normalizing the wire format away because daemon integration and CLI consumers already rely on them.

Legacy read tolerance is intentionally asymmetric with sanitized writes. serde(default) accepts older payloads with missing current fields, and unknown historical command/args/env/working_dir details are ignored rather than reintroduced into TextAdapterSummary. The strengthened regression feeds secret-looking values through all four historical detail fields and verifies the deserialized object's Debug representation retains none of them, demonstrating they are discarded at the protocol boundary rather than merely omitted during reserialization.

The public Debug surface of current text-adapter diagnostics is therefore limited to the same sanitized fields as serialization. Adapter ids and kind strings are machine identifiers intended to be user-visible, pid is explicitly part of local runtime diagnostics, and no selected text, ASR transcript, LLM response, command argument, environment value, or filesystem working-directory path is represented by these types.

lib.rs documentation was updated from migration-era wording that described the Rust daemon as future work. It now states the current shared daemon/CLI/GUI/Fcitx boundary, distinguishes required legacy wire compatibility from Vinpst-only extensions, and documents that diagnostic extensions use sanitized summary types. The other re-exported protocol modules remain unchanged and continue under their existing ownership units.

Evidence includes complete source review of lib.rs and text.rs; producer and CLI/D-Bus consumer inspection; sanitized JSON/schema tests, tolerant legacy/missing-field tests, the strengthened legacy secret-retention Debug regression, all 34 vinpst-protocol tests, strict all-target Clippy, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only PCM invariants, serialization boundary, and audio facade
notes: This is a current-only ownership unit for the remaining vinpst-audio facade/core file. PipeWire capture lifecycle is already owned by AUDIO-CAPTURE-001, source discovery by PIPEWIRE-DEVICE-001, and gain/quiet-normalization algebra by AUDIO-UTILS-001. This unit therefore owns the validated PCM value types, raw PCM and RIFF/WAVE decoding, frame/chunk helpers, capture traits and compatibility adapters, deterministic mock sources/recorders/enumerators, public AudioError surface, and crate-level API boundary without double-owning those previously audited behaviors.

The audit found a real invariant bypass in PcmBuffer's public serde contract. All normal constructors call with_spec, which rejects zero sample rate, zero channels, and sample counts that do not contain complete interleaved frames. The former derived Deserialize implementation populated the private spec/samples fields directly, so external JSON could construct channels=0 or sample_rate_hz=0 buffers and later make frame_len or duration_ms divide by zero, or create an unaligned multi-channel buffer that violates chunking assumptions.

PcmBuffer now keeps the same serialized {spec,samples} wire shape but implements Deserialize through a private wire helper followed by PcmBuffer::with_spec. Deterministic regressions prove a valid stereo buffer round-trips unchanged and malformed JSON is rejected for zero sample rate, zero channels, and an odd number of samples for a two-channel layout. CapturedAudio derives its deserialization through this validated PcmBuffer boundary, so nested payloads cannot bypass the same invariants.

The public PcmBuffer Debug implementation was also hardened before v0.1.0. The previous derived Debug expanded every signed PCM sample, which means any future diagnostic that formatted a PcmBuffer or CapturedAudio could disclose raw recorded speech content even though no current production logging call site does so. Debug now exposes only the validated PcmSpec and samples_len; a regression uses distinctive sample values and proves neither value appears in the rendered Debug output. CapturedAudio's derived Debug inherits that redaction for its PCM field while retaining non-content source metadata.

PcmSpec remains independently deserializable for compatibility, including the established default-to-mono behavior when channels is absent; PcmBuffer validation is the point where a layout becomes paired with sample storage. PcmChunkRange remains a simple serializable frame-coordinate value: its sample_range helper is private and current production slicing consumes only ranges generated by PcmBuffer::chunk_ranges_by_frames, so arbitrary deserialized ranges cannot be injected into the internal indexing path through the public API.

Raw PCM decoding continues to reject odd byte counts before constructing samples. RIFF/WAVE parsing remains strict about RIFF/WAVE identity, PCM format, 16-bit samples, fmt/data layout, byte rate/block alignment, chunk bounds and padding, then delegates final sample-rate/channel/alignment validation to PcmBuffer::with_spec. The source/recorder adapters preserve the deterministic compatibility boundary between one-shot AudioSource consumers and stateful AudioRecorder implementations, while mock implementations keep lifecycle failures explicit for tests.

The crate-level documentation was updated from obsolete migration text claiming the real PipeWire layer had not landed. It now describes the actual v0.1.0 boundary: validated PCM and decoding/processing contracts plus capture traits/test doubles, with the optional PipeWire backend implementing those contracts rather than being future work.

Evidence includes complete source review of vinpst-audio lib.rs and tests.rs; repository-wide PcmBuffer/PcmChunkRange producer-consumer and Debug/log call-site searches; the three new serde/Debug regressions, the complete vinpst-audio all-target test suite, PipeWire-feature compilation/tests, strict all-target Clippy, downstream ASR/daemon compile checks, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only shared provider HTTP client, bounded bodies, and safe diagnostics
notes: This is a current-only shared transport unit. Frozen HTTP behavior was embedded independently in remote ASR, text/OpenAI, registry, and GUI call sites; Vinpst centralizes the provider-facing client and bounded response reader in vinpst-http. Consumer-specific request schemas, endpoint construction, authorization headers, and response parsing remain owned by their ASR/text/GUI units; this audit claims only the common trust, redirect, timeout, body-limit, and diagnostic primitives.

Provider clients use reqwest blocking mode with rustls-tls and its built-in trust roots. SSL_CERT_FILE is additive rather than replacing the built-in roots: a non-empty path must open as a regular file, is bounded to 4 MiB before parsing, must contain at least one PEM certificate, and every parsed certificate is added as an extra root. HttpClientError intentionally stores only fixed error categories, so neither certificate paths, certificate bytes, nor lower-level parser/build details survive into Display or Debug.

Redirects are disabled at the shared ClientBuilder boundary. This keeps bearer/API credentials and POST bodies bound to the configured endpoint for remote ASR, OpenAI-compatible text/model discovery, and fetch_json_text consumers; a 3xx response therefore remains an ordinary non-success status instead of being automatically followed. The JSON fetch regression proves a 302 is returned as Status(302), and prior remote ASR/text audits own their endpoint-specific fail-closed handling.

Provider response reading is capped at exactly 1 MiB of bytes exposed by reqwest. The implementation reads through max+1 so an exactly-at-limit body succeeds and the next byte fails deterministically, rejects invalid UTF-8, and maps both direct and nested io/reqwest timeout causes to TimedOut while collapsing other read failures to the fixed Read category. No error variant stores the response body, request URL, or transport error object.

fetch_json_text applies a caller-supplied complete request deadline, accepts only success statuses, then delegates to the same bounded UTF-8 reader. reqwest_error_category similarly converts reqwest errors into fixed URL-free strings such as timed out, connection failed, request failed, or response decode failed. Remote ASR and OpenAI-compatible text use these shared helpers directly; GUI startup notifications use fetch_json_text and deliberately collapse its already-safe detailed category to a silent fetch failure.

Call-site review found no second provider-client construction path in those consumers that bypasses this shared redirect/trust/body policy. OpenAI-compatible text deliberately uses the connect-timeout variant so a TCP connection attempt cannot consume its longer overall deadline; remote ASR uses the default shared client plus its own request timeout. Registry transport remains separately owned by vinpst-registry because it has distinct cache/mirror semantics rather than being forced through this provider-response helper.

Evidence includes complete vinpst-http source/test review; workspace reqwest feature verification; repository-wide call-site inspection for every exported helper/limit; redirect, certificate-path/content redaction, CA-size, exact body-limit, invalid UTF-8, and nested-timeout tests; the complete vinpst-http all-target suite, strict all-target Clippy, downstream ASR/text/GUI compile checks, secret scan, and the module-parity ledger checker. No production-code change was required.

audits.title: Current-only ASR facade, remote diagnostics, timeout capability, mocks, and fallbacks
notes: This current-only unit owns the remaining vinpst-asr facade/runtime files after command, sherpa/offline/online/VAD, result, factory-state, and HTTP transport responsibilities were audited elsewhere. It covers the common AsrError surface, public crate re-exports, deterministic mock backend, OpenAI-compatible remote backend/session wrapper, timeout-capability diagnostics, and unavailable-backend placeholder without re-owning the already-audited command/sherpa implementations or the shared vinpst-http client primitive.

The audit found a real diagnostic-disclosure gap in remote non-success handling. ReqwestRemoteAsrTransport previously read every non-2xx provider body and appended it to AsrError::Backend after replacing only exact occurrences of the configured API key and prompt. Arbitrary provider-returned request ids, internal paths, echoed third-party credentials, or other body data could therefore propagate through RuntimeError into daemon last_error, CLI errors, and D-Bus failure details even though those values were unknown to the local redactor.

Remote non-success handling is now status-only. Once response headers reveal a non-success status, the transport returns `remote ASR provider returned HTTP <status>` without reading the body. This also means a slow or oversized 3xx/4xx/5xx body cannot convert the already-known HTTP failure into a later response-body timeout/size diagnostic. Redirects remain disabled by the shared HTTP client, so a 307 is reported by status and its Location target is still never contacted. Successful responses continue through the shared UTF-8 1 MiB bounded reader and retain distinct request-versus-success-body timeout diagnostics.

The deterministic remote-network smoke was updated to enforce that contract for 307, 429, 503, and oversized 503 bodies: status must remain visible while fixture body markers and the old error-body size diagnostic must remain absent. Its WAV fixture was also repaired from 0.25 seconds/4000 samples to one second/16000 samples because the already-established upstream-compatible MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_RECOGNITION gate is 8000; the old fixture silently skipped inference and therefore stopped exercising any network path. This is a test-fixture correction, not a change to the runtime minimum-audio policy.

RemoteAsrSpec and RemoteAsrRequest already use custom Debug representations that redact URL userinfo/query values, API keys, prompts, and raw WAV bytes while retaining model/language/timeout/size diagnostics. A live RemoteRecognitionSession additionally owns accumulated raw PCM and RecognitionContext selected text, so its unnecessary derived Debug implementation was removed entirely. This prevents a future diagnostic formatter from bypassing the request/spec redaction boundary by expanding the private live session object.

UnavailableAsrBackend intentionally preserves a backend-construction failure reason so create_session can report why an unavailable provider cannot be used; that user-visible behavior remains unchanged. Its derived Debug previously duplicated the preserved reason verbatim, however, so Debug now exposes only `error: <redacted>`. A regression proves the distinctive preserved reason remains available through create_session while it is absent from Debug.

timeout.rs is not a detached timeout runner and is intentionally retained. AsrTimeoutProbe classifies configured provider timeout behavior for `vinpst system doctor`: command providers report supervised process-deadline enforcement, remote providers report HTTP request enforcement, local/native providers report diagnostic-only unsupported enforcement, and absent timeout remains NotConfigured. Call-site review confirms the CLI doctor consumes this probe; it does not claim to impose a second timeout around recognition sessions.

The common AsrError variants were reviewed for disclosure and control-flow semantics. Structured variants contain only status/layout values or static state descriptions; Io retains ordinary std::io::Error detail; Backend(String) is intentionally flexible for implementation diagnostics, so producer boundaries must sanitize any remote or secret-bearing source before constructing it. The remote provider body fix closes the identified external-body path, while command-process and factory producer sanitization remain under their existing audit units.

MockAsrBackend remains deterministic test/development infrastructure. Its audio log stores push kind, sample count, and PCM spec rather than sample values, while configured mock transcripts/events are explicit caller-provided fixtures. unavailable.rs and mock.rs therefore require no wire or behavioral compatibility changes beyond the unavailable Debug hardening. The crate-level documentation was updated from migration-era future-backend wording to the actual local/command/remote/mock/unavailable backend set and capability-diagnostic role.

Evidence includes complete review of the six owned files plus factory/trait/runtime/CLI-doctor call chains; the new status-only unknown-provider-secret regression, unavailable Debug regression, all 153 vinpst-asr tests, deterministic proxy/NO_PROXY/auth/TLS/redirect/error/timeout/body-limit network smoke, ShellCheck with sourced helpers, strict all-target Clippy, daemon/CLI downstream compile checks, docs build, secret scan, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only text facade, command adapter wire, and diagnostic redaction
notes: This current-only unit owns the remaining vinpst-text facade, common TextError surface, and command-adapter request/response/registry/processor file. Core scene dispatch, OpenAI-compatible transport, payload fallback, prompt interpolation, context cache, and long-lived adapter runtime remain under their earlier ownership units and are supporting evidence here rather than being claimed again.

The audit found the same external-body disclosure class previously fixed for remote ASR. OpenAI-compatible text transport read every non-success provider body and inserted it into TextError::AdapterFailed after replacing only known Authorization values, so arbitrary provider-returned request ids, internal paths, or unknown credentials could reach daemon warnings and CLI diagnostics. Non-success responses are now status-only and their bodies are left unread; successful responses retain the shared 1 MiB UTF-8 limit and request/response-body timeout classification.

The production `vinpst llm test` loopback smoke now proves both sides of that boundary: a normal authenticated /v1/chat/completions request still returns the expected payload, while a deterministic 503 exposes HTTP status but neither the configured API key nor an unknown provider-body marker. Shared proxy/TLS/redirect/body-limit evidence remains correctly classified as local deterministic evidence, not hosted-service proof.

CommandTextRequest, CommandTextScene, CommandTextResponse, CommandTextAdapter, AdapterRegistry, and CommandTextProcessor previously derived Debug across data that can include raw ASR text, selected text, scene prompts, generated response text, command arguments, environment values, and working-directory paths. Their Debug implementations now expose only stable ids plus lengths/counts/booleans and safe scene metadata. JSON serialization is unchanged, so configured local helpers still receive the complete request body they require and responses still deserialize into the same payload contract.

A supporting config-schema hardening was discovered because text adapter/provider wrappers also derive or compose Debug over typed config. Registry URLs, ASR provider command/env/path fields, LLM API keys/extra bodies, adapter command/env/working directories, and scene prompts now have secret-safe typed Debug representations; parent config Debug automatically inherits those representations. That fix was committed independently because schema ownership belongs to the earlier config audit rather than this text unit.

Local command helper stderr intentionally keeps different semantics from remote provider bodies. The helper is a user-configured local executable, its stdout/stderr are concurrently drained under the shared process supervisor with 1 MiB caps and deadlines, and a bounded nonzero-exit stderr remains useful local diagnostics. This unit does not claim generic secret detection for arbitrary user programs; it only prevents Vinpst's own Debug surfaces from duplicating command configuration or text contents.

Migration-era wording was corrected without changing behavior: the explicit unavailable text/command runners are fallbacks rather than promises that adapters have not landed, recent-input context wiring is already available to provider request builders, and crate documentation now describes the actual command/OpenAI-compatible/prompt/context functionality present before v0.1.0.

Evidence includes complete review of command.rs/error.rs/lib.rs plus their producer/consumer call chains; strengthened request/response/adapter Debug regressions; status-only unknown-provider-secret unit and production-CLI 503 fixture; all 138 vinpst-text tests; strict all-target Clippy, downstream daemon/CLI/GUI compile checks, ShellCheck, docs build, secret scan, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only registry schema, planning, and provider-script facade
notes: This current-only unit owns the remaining generic vinpst-registry facade, validation schema/error surface, dry-run asset/install planning, and provider-script editor boundary. Download/cache/live-model/live-script/archive/checksum/materialization/operation behavior remains under its earlier audit units and is supporting call-chain context rather than being re-owned here.

The audit found a credential disclosure in dry-run planning. PlannedAsset and PlannedInstallAsset stored fully resolved candidate URLs and derived both Serialize and Debug; registry plan JSON and hidden model/adapter install-plan JSON serialize these structures directly. A registry mirror carrying userinfo or query credentials could therefore be printed verbatim even though the downloader itself needs the unredacted URL only in memory.

Planning now keeps the original candidate URLs unchanged in memory for download/staging consumers while custom Serialize and Debug use the shared URL redactor for parsed URLs. Userinfo, fragments, and query values are therefore absent from dry-run JSON and Debug, while scheme/host/port/path/query-key shape remains actionable. Legacy opaque mirrors made only from safe path characters remain visible rather than degrading to <invalid-url>; suspicious unparseable values are fail-closed. A regression proves the in-memory plan still contains the credential-bearing request URL while serialized/debug forms do not.

The same review exposed a functional URL-joining bug for an otherwise valid configured mirror with query or fragment components. The previous string concatenation placed the asset path after `?` or `#`, so it became query/fragment text instead of a request path. Parsed http(s) URLs now append the registry-relative asset to the URL path while preserving userinfo, query, and fragment for the actual request; opaque/non-URL mirror strings retain the legacy trailing-slash string fallback.

RegistryIndex, ModelEntry, AdapterEntry, and AssetEntry contain manifest ids/labels/provider-kind metadata, relative validated asset paths, checksums, and sizes but no configured mirror URL or credential values, so their ordinary derived Debug/Serialize remain appropriate. RegistryError was reviewed variant by variant and carries parse detail, ids, relative asset paths, or checksum text; no API key, environment value, candidate URL, or response-body producer was found in this owned error surface.

Provider-script editing intentionally keeps explicit user-facing editor/path output: `provider edit-script --json` reports the exact editor argv and script path requested for that operation, and editor launch failures name the selected editor command. Internal Debug no longer duplicates filesystem paths, HOME/current-directory values, or editor arguments from VINPST_PROVIDER_EDITOR/VISUAL/EDITOR; context/editor/plan/outcome Debug exposes only provider id, counts, booleans, and exit status. Direct argv execution and shell-free parsing remain unchanged.

The crate facade re-exports the already-audited registry primitives without introducing an alternate side-effect path. Its documentation accurately describes registry manifest, URL resolution, staged asset, archive/materialization, and provider-script boundaries; configuration mutation and user-facing CLI routing remain outside this crate.

Evidence includes complete review of error.rs/lib.rs/plan.rs/provider_script.rs/schema.rs and CLI/staging consumers; credentialed plan JSON/Debug regressions, query/fragment path-join regression, provider-script Debug regression, full vinpst-registry tests, strict all-target Clippy, focused CLI provider/registry/model/adapter tests, downstream CLI/GUI compile checks, docs build, secret scan, diff check, and the module-parity ledger checker.

Follow-up managed-script review tightened the provider-script facade from `metadata` to `symlink_metadata` when resolving editable command/argument candidates. Edit Script now accepts only an existing regular file and does not follow a symlink placed at the configured managed path; a Unix regression pins the fail-closed behavior. Direct editor argv execution and the existing redacted Debug/error boundary remain unchanged.

audits.title: Current-only registry CLI routing, source diagnostics, and live fetch glue
notes: This current-only unit owns the standalone `vinpst registry` Clap surface, its local-index validate/plan/install-plan command implementation, and the CLI glue shared by live model/provider/adapter registry loading. Generic command aggregation, domain-specific model/provider/adapter presentation, registry transport/cache implementations, and live i18n remain supporting responsibilities rather than being re-owned here.

The audit found a second registry-URL correctness gap after REGISTRY-FACADE-001. CLI live registry and CLI/registry i18n paths still had independent string-concatenation helpers, so a valid configured mirror containing query or fragment components placed `registry/*.json` or `i18n/*.json` after `?`/`#` instead of in the URL path. The registry crate now exports one resolve_registry_url policy used by asset planning, live registry catalogs, CLI i18n, and best-effort registry i18n refresh; parsed URLs preserve userinfo/query/fragment for requests while opaque mirrors keep the existing string fallback.

The same call-chain review found a user-visible credential disclosure. Raw configured `registry_urls` and the successful cache layer `fresh_url` flowed into model/provider/adapter source JSON, model human source labels, validation context strings, and cached/uncached i18n source diagnostics. A mirror such as `https://user:pass@host/root?token=...` could therefore be fetched correctly but then printed back to the terminal or JSON output with its credentials.

Request and diagnostic representations are now separated. Network fetches still receive the exact configured URL, while registry_url_for_diagnostics removes URL userinfo/fragments, replaces query values with REDACTED, preserves safe opaque mirrors, and fails closed for suspicious unparseable values.
