FetchedText stores only a sanitized resolved source because every consumer uses that field for presentation/parse context rather than a subsequent request; source JSON also projects the complete mirror list through the same diagnostic helper.

Explicit local `--registry` files are covered too. Although no network request occurs in that mode, model/provider/adapter source JSON previously copied mirrors from the selected config verbatim as metadata. Those rows now use registry_urls_for_diagnostics, so choosing a local registry cannot become an accidental credential-dump command. Bare `vinpst registry` similarly projects its bundled index URLs through the diagnostic boundary even though bundled mirrors are expected to be public.

Remote registry i18n had both cached and uncached raw-URL presentation paths. Both now keep the raw URL only for RegistryTextSource::fetch_registry_text and use the diagnostic projection for layer JSON and source labels. A deterministic fake-source regression proves the requests still carry the original credentialed/query URL while the resulting diagnostics contain only the redacted URL shape.

registry_support.rs also owns the managed-script transaction helper used by provider/adapter installs. Its pre-update symlink/non-regular-file rejection, same-directory backup, rollback after install or config-write failure, and cleanup behavior were reviewed against existing process tests; this URL hardening does not alter those side-effect semantics. LoadedLiveScriptRegistry/FetchedText deliberately do not derive Debug over registry bodies or raw request state.

The typed RegistryCommand surface remains intentionally compact: model/adapter selectors are mutually exclusive at Clap parse time, summary-only removes per-asset rows, validate reads only the explicit local index, and install-plan is side-effect free. Runtime errors retain the previously audited generic JSON/text error formatting rather than introducing a second registry-specific error envelope.

Evidence includes full-file review of cli/registry.rs, commands/registry.rs, and registry_support.rs plus model/provider/adapter/i18n consumers; shared URL join and diagnostic helper regressions, an uncached remote-i18n raw-request-versus-redacted-diagnostic test, a process-level credentialed-config plus local-registry model-list JSON test, registry/provider/model/adapter CLI suites, strict CLI/registry Clippy, downstream compile checks, docs build, secret scan, diff check, and the module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only CLI command facade and hidden config fixtures
notes: commands/mod.rs is a crate-internal aggregation facade only: it declares the already-audited domain command modules and re-exports their handlers/types to main.rs. It does not define a second parser, formatter, transport, config mutation, or side-effect path, and the complete root/help-surface tests remain the authority for which commands are user-visible.

config_examples.rs embeds three committed JSON fixtures by compile-time include_str: the ordinary default skeleton plus deterministic command-demo and configured PipeWire-live fixtures. `init` consumes only ConfigExample::Default; the two e2e fixtures are available through the explicit config-example maintenance surface for deterministic tests and live validation.

The config-example command is already hidden from ordinary help with #[command(hide = true)], and the help-surface regression requires it to remain registered but hidden. This matches the v0.1.0 CLI policy that test/maintenance mechanisms stay script-compatible without cluttering the user-facing interface.

Export is not blind file copying: commands/config.rs reparses the embedded text as VinpstConfig, validates it, and only then prints or writes it. The three included JSON files parse as JSON and their existing process tests cover list, command-demo stdout, and configured-PipeWire file export; invalid future fixture drift therefore fails tests rather than silently becoming a published example.

No credentials are synthesized or loaded by this facade. Descriptions contain only stable fixture purpose text, the command facade carries no runtime data, and the embedded examples are repository fixtures rather than environment-derived user configuration. Existing config validation/diagnostic redaction remains outside this unit and is not bypassed by example export.

Evidence includes full review of commands/mod.rs and config_examples.rs, their parser/handler/init/config-IO call chains, the hidden-maintenance help regression, all three config-example process tests, strict all-target CLI Clippy, JSON parsing of every embedded fixture, diff check, and module-parity ledger validation.

audits.title: Current-only CLI diagnostics, activation service, and guarded daemon lifecycle
notes: This current-only unit owns the remaining CLI system diagnostics/activation-service implementation plus user-systemd service installation, guarded package-upgrade handoff, and guarded package-removal handoff. Generic systemctl command construction, daemon status/procfs inspection, sandbox host wrapping, atomic file primitives, and package session discovery remain supporting responsibilities under their earlier audit units.

The activation-service review found a persistence inconsistency. Per-user D-Bus activation metadata used fs::write directly even though other persistent control files use same-directory atomic replacement; a failed write could therefore leave a truncated service. It now uses the shared write_file_atomically path, which synchronizes and renames a new file while resolving final symlink targets. A Unix process regression proves a relative dotfiles-style service symlink remains a symlink while the target receives the complete service atomically.

Activation-service status/removal also used Path::exists, which follows symlinks and reports a dangling service symlink as absent. That made a broken canonical link invisible to --user-status and impossible to repair with --remove-user. Presence now uses symlink_metadata: status reports the directory entry as present plus the target read error, and removal deletes the dangling symlink itself. A process regression covers both diagnosis and repair.

The upgrade-handoff audit found that the stale-systemd branch bypassed the idle/no-active-session guard already enforced for direct-owner handoff and for package removal. This contradicted the packaging contract and could restart a stale systemd-owned daemon during an active recording. A matching MainPID is now only eligible for daemon-reload/restart when the live D-Bus snapshot is idle with active_session=false; guard refusal performs no systemd mutation and records an explicit systemd_guard result.

The same path had a release-transaction propagation bug: daemon handoff printed an `ok:false` JSON object for guard/control/verification failures but still returned process success. package-upgrade-handoff.sh intentionally relies on the CLI exit status, so a daemon-reload/restart/guard failure could be counted as a successful package handoff. Non-dry-run handoff now preserves the diagnostic JSON/text and returns a failing exit status whenever its result is not ok; dry-run remains successful and non-mutating.

The isolated-bus handoff smoke now proves the complete sequence on one stale systemd owner: an active mock recording is rejected with nonzero exit, systemd_guard shows the busy state, and neither daemon-reload nor restart runs; after StopRecording returns the owner to idle, the same handoff reloads/restarts and verifies the replacement owner. The existing daemon-reload failure case was strengthened to require nonzero exit while preserving the old owner. Current-owner no-op and guarded direct-owner replacement remain covered in the same smoke.

Removal was reviewed separately rather than assumed equivalent. It reloads D-Bus activation metadata before every preflight/execution, performs zero-mutation two-phase preflight, rejects busy systemd owners with removal_session_guard, reuses the strict UID/PID/start-time/executable/cgroup guard plus identity revalidation for direct owners, verifies owner absence after mutation, and propagates nonzero on unsafe completion. Existing private-bus removal and cross-user package rollback smokes continue to pass unchanged.

install-service already used the atomic writer, renders the Flatpak host unit through the separately audited sandbox policy, reloads the user manager only after successful installation, and reports a reload failure as an error while leaving the complete installed unit available for retry. Its dry-run remains the package/Flatpak proof surface and does not write or reload.

commands/system.rs diagnostic outputs were reviewed for data boundaries. protocol/ASR/audio/doctor paths expose explicit machine/config/model/service/addon diagnostics but use the previously audited config summary and ASR error boundaries rather than API-key/environment values; next-step interpolation uses provider ids only. User activation Exec/path and Fcitx addon paths are intentionally returned only by explicit maintenance/doctor diagnostics, not ordinary root help.

Evidence includes complete source review of all four owned files; 39 protocol process tests including atomic symlink write/dangling repair and dry-run guard policy; strict all-target CLI Clippy; isolated D-Bus upgrade handoff with busy-systemd zero-mutation, idle systemd restart, direct-owner replacement, and daemon-reload failure propagation; guarded removal smoke; cross-user package upgrade and removal/rollback smokes; ShellCheck for the changed handoff script; packaging-contract update; full CLI gate, docs, secret scan, diff check, and module-parity ledger validation. These private-session smokes are deterministic process proof, not a substitute for the separately tracked real desktop/systemd live gate.

audits.title: Current-only daemon runtime menus, diagnostics, persistence, and facade
notes: This current-only unit owns the remaining small daemon runtime glue files after recording/reload/adapter/remote/D-Bus protocol behavior was audited in earlier units. It covers the public daemon facade, ASR provider/model menu projection, capture and scene mutation helpers, daemon-local config persistence wrapper, runtime diagnostic JSON projection, and common RuntimeError surface without re-owning the larger runtime state machine or D-Bus service.

The audit found a raw-user-text disclosure in the Vinpst-only GetRuntimeStatus diagnostic extension. runtime_status_json() was documented as sanitized but serialized partial_text verbatim while selected text was already represented only by selected_text_present. Because daemon status and GetRuntimeStatus are diagnostic/status surfaces rather than recognition-result delivery, the snapshot now exposes partial_text_present only. RecognitionPartial and stop-result paths retain the actual partial text where it is the requested functional payload.

A regression injects a distinctive partial transcript directly into RuntimeState and proves the status JSON reports presence without containing either a partial_text field or the transcript marker. Existing D-Bus integration already proves selected command text is absent from GetRuntimeStatus, so both transient user-text sources now follow the same diagnostic disclosure policy.

The audit also found a second atomic-config implementation in runtime/config_io.rs. It validated callers before use and wrote a synchronized temporary file, but unlike the shared vinpst-config persistence boundary it renamed over a symlink entry, used a PID-only temporary filename, and inherited existing permissions instead of enforcing the current private-config policy. Scene, capture-device, and ASR target D-Bus mutations all passed through this weaker helper.

Daemon mutations now delegate to vinpst_config::write_config_file, retaining no-backup semantics for these targeted D-Bus changes while gaining the already-audited typed validation, bounded unique temporary creation, 0600 file mode on Unix, complete-file sync, cleanup, and safe resolution of symlink write targets. RuntimeError now wraps ConfigWriteError instead of maintaining separate serialization/I/O variants. A daemon-local regression proves a relative config symlink remains a symlink while its target receives the updated config.

ASR menu helpers were reviewed end to end with SetActiveAsrTarget. They expose only configured provider ids/kinds, stable or basename-derived model ids/titles, concrete model values required to make a selection, and the already-audited reload state. Broken installed model metadata is filtered, local installed-model values must match scanned managed models unless they are already the configured value, unknown provider/model pairs fail before persistence, and display-title locale candidates are de-duplicated in environment priority order.

Scene and capture mutations remain Idle-only, clone and validate the complete candidate config, persist before mutating runtime state when a config path exists, and update only in-memory state when running from an ephemeral config. Scene labels preserve Raw/Command compatibility fallbacks; CaptureTarget owns capture-device normalization and validation. No additional state-transition gap was found.

The RuntimeError surface was reviewed by producer. ASR/text errors inherit their already-hardened status-only/secret-safe boundaries, installed-model errors contain managed filesystem metadata rather than credential values, BackgroundTask is constructed from Tokio join state, and config errors now inherit ConfigWriteError/ConfigError redaction. The frozen-compatible AsrBackendState.last_error field remains unchanged; this unit only removes raw transcript content from the additive runtime-status snapshot.

Evidence includes complete source and call-site review of the seven owned files; focused partial-status and config-symlink regressions; existing ASR menu/scene/capture tests; full vinpst-daemon unit/CLI/D-Bus/remote suites; strict all-target Clippy; downstream vinpst-cli daemon-status tests; synchronization of two stale daemon expectations with the already-audited typed text-adapter error contract; docs build, secret scan, diff check, and module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only GUI daemon queries, reload confirmation, errors, guards, and provider-script editing
notes: This current-only unit owns five small GUI operation boundaries left pending after the page-level audits: required/optional daemon snapshot queries, ASR reload confirmation polling, top-level recoverable-error presentation, cross-form mutation guards, and managed provider-script editor integration. Larger hotword/script/model state machines remain supporting files for later ownership rather than being absorbed here.

The audit removed a protocol-drift hazard in ASR reload confirmation. asr_reload_confirmation.rs carried a second hand-written decoder for the exact eight-field GetAsrBackendState tuple even though daemon_client.rs already owns the same typed conversion. Reload confirmation now reuses daemon_client::query_asr_backend_state, so Control-page live state and hotword reload confirmation cannot silently diverge if the additive Rust D-Bus decoder changes.

Reload confirmation remains intentionally blocking only inside blocking_task workers. It first requests ReloadAsrBackend, polls the typed backend state for at most 60 seconds, waits while reload_in_progress is true, rejects target supersession, treats non-empty last_error as failure even when effective ids look unchanged, and uses RequestedAsrBackendStatus to distinguish applied from previous-backend/no-backend/config-saved/unknown outcomes. Raw backend error detail is not copied into the GUI confirmation message.

daemon_client.rs keeps required guards and optional diagnostics separate. GetStatus and GetRuntimeStatus must succeed and parse for a usable DaemonSnapshot; unsupported/invalid text-adapter state defaults to an empty diagnostic state and optional ASR backend state is omitted rather than failing the whole snapshot. query_daemon_snapshot_if_owned checks NameHasOwner before creating the service proxy path, preserving the non-activating polling behavior used by owner monitoring and daemon controls.

The audit found two user-facing GUI disclosure/localization gaps. Managed provider-script success text previously echoed the entire editor argv selected from VINPST_PROVIDER_EDITOR/VISUAL/EDITOR, and launch/exit errors could echo the same command through ProviderScriptEditError. GUI success now reports only the provider id and explicit managed script path; launch/exit errors are localized generic messages that retain only safe exit status. The CLI explicit edit-script plan/error contract is intentionally unchanged.

The exact-managed-script guard remains strict: GUI editing is offered only for the managed command-provider path derived from current config, provider-script resolution must return that exact path, and the editor is executed directly without a shell. The script path remains visible because the user explicitly chose Edit Script and needs to know which managed file changed; editor argv is unnecessary presentation metadata and is now omitted.

form_guards.rs previously emitted hard-coded English text inside an otherwise localized GUI when an LLM or ASR provider editor blocked a resource mutation. Those guard messages now route through GuiLocale with English and zh_CN forms. The broader application still permits typed lower-level errors to retain technical English diagnostics; this fix targets GUI-authored guard copy rather than inventing a second translation taxonomy for every dependency error.

error_dialog.rs remains a simple modal projection rather than an error parser: it shows one recoverable message as plain Iced text, offers Retry only for retryable model/script install failures, and otherwise offers Dismiss. No markup/shell interpretation or hidden retry side effect was found. The existing OperationState and install state machines remain the owners of retry eligibility.

Evidence includes complete source/call-site review of the five owned files; exact reload classification regression; provider-script exact-path and real editor execution tests; new editor-argument redaction regression in both locales; localized dynamic-form and open-editor guard tests; strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy; the full GUI suite; the updated GUI contract documenting that environment-derived editor argv is not presentation data; docs build, secret scan, diff check, and module-parity ledger checker.

audits.title: Current-only daemon owner reconciliation and keyboard interaction baseline
notes: This current-only unit owns the GUI daemon-owner signal monitor, global keyboard interaction mapping, and the bounded custom focus/activation widget wrapper. These responsibilities have no one-to-one frozen Qt files because they arise from the Rust/Iced event model and the explicit 0.1.0 keyboard-accessibility policy; page actions and daemon query/control implementations remain under their existing units.

Daemon owner reconciliation subscribes to the filtered NameOwnerChanged stream before sampling NameHasOwner, avoiding the registration-versus-snapshot race. Connected/Changed events invalidate any earlier refresh generation; owner loss immediately marks the daemon Stopped and stale worker completions are rejected by operation id. Owner return starts one fresh snapshot query without showing a transient loading shell.

If the owner signal stream fails, the GUI records an internal Failed monitor state and switches to serialized 30-second fallback polling. The poll calls query_daemon_snapshot_if_owned, which checks NameHasOwner before constructing the service snapshot and therefore does not activate a stopped daemon. Only one refresh id may be active at a time; a later owner signal or explicit restart invalidates the earlier worker result. The stored monitor failure string is not presented as daemon state or a user-facing notification.

A real private dbus-daemon test proves filtered name acquisition and loss signals rather than mocking the event sequence. Application-state regressions prove stale snapshots cannot resurrect a lost owner, owner return recovers automatically, monitor failure retains the last good snapshot until the non-activating poll resolves, and repeated fallback ticks are serialized.

The interaction layer intentionally handles only non-repeating shortcuts not consumed by active widgets, except F6 which may be honored even when a widget captures the key so the registry workflow focus command remains dependable. Escape clears focus or dismisses the active modal/detail, Tab and Shift+Tab perform traversal, Command+1..4 switch the four stable pages, and ordinary text-editing combinations such as Command+C are not intercepted. Busy-state guards continue to block page switching while allowing focus traversal.

KeyboardAction wraps enabled pointer controls rather than replacing their pointer/overlay behavior. It participates in Iced focus operations with a visible focus ring, forwards every event to the underlying widget first, and only handles an uncaptured key when the wrapper itself is focused. Enter/Space activate buttons/checkboxes, arrows publish bounded previous/next selection messages, modifiers and key repeat are ignored, and disabled controls with no keyboard messages are returned unwrapped so they do not enter the custom focus order.

adjacent_values handles missing/current/end selections without indexing outside the option slice. Tests pin activation keys, arrow directions, modifiers/repeat rejection, missing selection fallback, and empty options; interaction tests pin shortcut mapping, modal/busy behavior, dynamic localized window titles, and the declared capability snapshot.

The capability snapshot matches the documented 0.1.0 accessibility contract: keyboard management, clipboard editing, and Wayland/X11 input-method handling are supported, while a platform assistive-technology semantic tree and screen-reader navigation are explicitly unsupported. CLI, fcitx5-configtool, guarded config-file editing, and fcitx reload commands remain documented fallbacks; this audit does not falsely upgrade toolkit capability.

Evidence includes complete source/call-site review of the three owned files; private-session D-Bus owner acquire/loss tests; daemon generation/fallback state tests; keyboard shortcut, focus, activation, adjacent-value, busy/modal, title, and capability-snapshot tests; the full 219-test vinpst-gui suite plus main test; strict all-target Clippy; docs build; and module-parity ledger validation.

audits.title: Current-only hotword path resolution, atomic publication, and activation retry
notes: This current-only unit owns the filesystem and retry primitives deliberately left supporting in the earlier Hotword-page audit: deterministic content-path resolution, conflict-aware snapshot/versioning and atomic publication, missing-file preparation, and the pending activation retry token. The page/editor state machine and typed HotwordMessage routing remain under their existing unit.

Path resolution is intentionally stricter than blindly applying the daemon working directory. Absolute configured hotword paths are directly editable; local providers may resolve a relative hotword only against an absolute existing model directory; relative model plus relative hotword is rejected because GUI and daemon process environments may differ. Command-provider relative paths are left to the external command and require an absolute path for GUI content editing, remote providers are rejected, and URL-like configured values are never treated as filesystem paths.

HotwordContentSnapshot bounds reads to 1 MiB, refuses symlinks/non-regular files, verifies the opened inode metadata against the path before reading and rechecks the path afterward, requires UTF-8, and rejects extended attributes/ACL metadata the GUI cannot preserve safely. Debug exposes only existence and a redacted content marker. The version tracks device/inode/size/uid/gid/mode/mtime/ctime; after claiming a file by hard link, comparison deliberately omits ctime because creating the recovery link itself changes ctime while preserving the actual loaded content/inode contract.

Publication uses a same-directory create_new temporary file, verifies ownership compatibility, writes and syncs the complete content, restores exact special permission bits for existing files, and validates the prepared snapshot. A missing target publishes with rename NOREPLACE. An existing target is first preserved as an adjacent hard-link recovery file and directory-synced, then current and preserved snapshots must still match the loaded baseline before Linux rename exchange is attempted.

After exchange both sides are verified: the configured path must match the prepared new snapshot and the displaced temporary path must still match the loaded old snapshot. If an external race invalidates the exchange, rollback is attempted only while the configured path still matches the GUI-published snapshot; otherwise configured path, displaced file, and recovery link are preserved rather than overwriting an external update. Cleanup/directory-sync failures are reported as post-publication durability errors instead of falsely claiming rollback.

Publishing content intentionally establishes a no-automatic-rollback boundary before daemon activation. The code snapshots the just-published file, attempts reload, re-reads it, and only creates retryable pending activation when reload failed and the file is still exactly the published baseline. A concurrent post-publication file change disables retry and is surfaced explicitly; the GUI never replaces that external version merely to restore the pre-edit file.

Missing-file preparation for a hotword-path config mutation likewise uses NOREPLACE and occurs only after config mutation preflight. If the later config save/reload fails, the newly prepared file is preserved rather than deleted because a safe rollback cannot prove it was not concurrently adopted or changed by another process. This conservative behavior is explicitly reflected in the returned error.

PendingHotwordActivation stores either the exact configured-path value or a path plus redacted content/version snapshot and has a custom Debug containing only provider id and target kind. Retry first verifies the loaded ConfigDocument is still current, the same provider is active, and the configured target/file baseline is unchanged; it reloads and waits for typed ASR confirmation; then it repeats the same validation before claiming success. Config-only retries intentionally do not claim file-content ownership.

The application call chain blocks RetryActivation while another operation is busy, assigns a hotword operation id to reject stale worker completion, clears pending state only on confirmed success or when a newly loaded/saved baseline supersedes it, and refreshes daemon state afterward. No additional race, rollback, or disclosure gap was found.

Evidence includes complete review of the three owned files and hotword-management call sites; path ambiguity tests; file-picker/path/content redaction tests; external config/file conflict tests; symlink/xattr/ownership/mode/size checks; NOREPLACE, hard-link recovery, exchange-race rollback, directory-sync, repeated recovery allocation, post-publication verification, and retry-version tests; the full 219-test GUI suite and strict Clippy; plus module-parity ledger validation.

audits.title: Current-only managed script catalog, publication, rollback, recovery, and removal transactions
notes: This current-only unit owns the remaining managed provider/text-adapter transaction layer beneath the already-audited Resources UI: registry catalog resolution, plan materialization, environment carry-forward, executable publication, adapter revision/rollback artifacts, config-only recovery after publication, guarded removal, and the App removal worker wrapper. The generic registry downloader/installer and page state machines remain under their earlier units.

The audit found the same query-bearing mirror bug previously fixed in the shared registry asset planner: script_management constructed providers.json/adapters.json with string concatenation, and the already-owned GUI model catalog did the same for models.json. Both now use vinpst_registry::resolve_registry_url so the registry path is inserted into the parsed URL path while userinfo/query/fragment remain request components; opaque mirror strings retain legacy slash concatenation. Dedicated GUI regressions cover provider, adapter, and model catalog URLs with query/fragment mirrors.

Preparation checks cancellation before and after registry work, verifies the loaded ConfigDocument is still mutation-safe, resolves an exact registry id/short id and deterministic managed relative path, materializes a prospective typed config before download, and pre-fills only registry-declared environment entries from an existing managed resource. Required environment values are validated before asset download; unrelated existing environment keys are preserved by materialization and only declared entries are updated.

Installation revalidates the document and environment contract, materializes and validates the complete candidate config, prepares adapter rollback state before publication, delegates download/publication to the already-audited registry installer, verifies the returned installed path equals the planned managed path, records the published adapter revision, and only then commits configuration through the shared validated atomic save plus daemon reconciliation boundary. Cancellation before publication is clean; publication followed by config failure has an explicit recovery/rollback outcome rather than a false Installed result.

The audit found the adapter rollback copy still used a PID-only temporary filename plus path-based fs::copy. A stale or planted temporary symlink could therefore redirect rollback preservation, and restore trusted the adjacent rollback artifact without proving it was still the revision captured before publication. The copy boundary now opens only an existing regular source file, verifies path/opened/final inode metadata across the read, allocates a bounded unique create_new sibling temporary file, writes through the held file descriptor, preserves source permissions, fsyncs file and parent directory, and atomically renames it into place.

ManagedScriptRollback now hashes the exact regular-file bytes it preserves. Restore reopens the rollback artifact through the same regular-file/version guard, verifies its SHA-256 still matches the captured rollback revision, and refuses to overwrite the published canonical script if the rollback file was replaced or modified. Published adapter revision calculation also uses the regular-file reader, so a post-install symlink swap cannot be accepted as the managed revision. Regressions cover a planted legacy PID-temp symlink, tampered rollback revision, and a symlinked canonical adapter path.

A related follow-up in the shared provider-script facade changed editable candidate inspection to symlink_metadata. Exact managed provider-script editing therefore remains direct-argv and path-exact but is now regular-file-only; a managed-path symlink is not followed into an arbitrary external target. This supporting fix is recorded on REGISTRY-FACADE-001 rather than double-owned here.

Config recovery is intentionally available only after a script has already been published and no adapter rollback transaction owns the prior version. It repeats config mutation and environment validation, requires the published path to still be a regular file, rematerializes the config, reapplies environment and managed adapter revision metadata, validates the complete config, and commits without re-downloading. Missing, directory, or symlink publication paths remain recovery failures; environment values stay redacted from outcome Debug.

Managed removal recognizes a resource only when its configured args are exactly the deterministic managed-root script path. Active ASR providers are refused; user-defined providers/adapters are not reclassified as managed; the complete config is validated and atomically committed before any script deletion. A config-save failure leaves both canonical and rollback artifacts intact. After a successful config commit, canonical/adapter rollback cleanup errors are reported in the success summary without pretending the now-unreferenced file was removed. Removing a symlink at the managed path uses remove_file and therefore unlinks only that managed entry rather than following its target.

The App removal wrapper preserves dirty Control, scene, LLM-provider, ASR-provider, and Hotword edits through explicit guards, blocks concurrent busy operations, runs filesystem/config work on the named blocking worker, reloads the ConfigDocument only after a successful removal transaction, and refreshes daemon state afterward. Worker-start failure is converted to a localized fixed category rather than raw environment/process detail.

Evidence includes complete source/call-site review of the four owned files; provider-script regular-file tests; query/fragment registry URL regressions for model/provider/adapter catalogs; rollback temp-symlink, revision-tamper, canonical-symlink and rejected-update restore tests; published-script recovery regular-file tests; managed provider/adapter removal and failed-config preservation tests; required environment and revision metadata tests; strict vinpst-registry/vinpst-gui all-target Clippy; full GUI suite; docs build; secret scan; diff check; and module-parity ledger validation.

audits.title: Current-only GUI composition root, central messages, ASR provider manager, and resource details
notes: This final current-only unit owns the four GUI composition files intentionally left supporting while page- and workflow-specific units were audited: the top-level App state/update/view/config boundary, the central Message/ConfigDraftMessage routing enum and busy classification, the ASR provider lifecycle manager behind its already-owned view, and the typed resource-detail modal projection. With this unit every current source file in the parity ledger has an explicit owner.

The App boot path validates or loads the bundled config, initializes a draft and Hotword editor from the same document, and batches independent daemon, notification, model catalog, audio-device, provider-catalog, and adapter-catalog startup tasks. The update path applies modal/removal/notification/desktop/daemon/adapter/ASR/script-removal interceptors before the global busy guard, then routes only unblocked messages; variants that must have been intercepted are unreachable at the central match. This preserves workflow-specific stale-operation and conflict guards without duplicating them at the root.

Subscriptions are similarly bounded: daemon owner reconciliation is always active, Control adds the two-second non-activating live-state poll, and model/script progress timers exist only while their worker state is active. Configuration replacement resets every form whose baseline may now be stale and refreshes the Hotword editor against the new typed document. Page/render composition stacks resource details, destructive confirmation, and failure dialogs above the base page instead of permitting underlying interaction through them.

The audit found a diagnostic composition gap: App still used derived Debug. Even though many nested domain types already redact credentials, App directly stores arbitrary resource-filter/model-filter text and OperationState success/failure strings and could therefore expose user-entered or lower-layer diagnostic text through a generic state dump. App now implements a deliberately non-exhaustive structural Debug containing only locale/page, filter lengths, config/daemon/operation state categories, draft dirtiness, safe model count, install activity, selected-resource kind, and editor/dialog/operation presence booleans. It never expands ConfigDocument, filter contents, operation text, selected resource ids/paths, or editor inputs.

A regression places distinctive secrets in both filters, an OperationState error, and an LLM provider URL/API key/extra body, formats the application state, and proves none of those markers appear while the structural failed-state and filter-length fields remain diagnosable. This closes the final GUI composition-root hole under DEBUG-LOG-001 rather than relying solely on every nested future field to remember its own redacted Debug implementation.

Central Message derives Debug because sensitive edit payloads are represented by SecretInput or message/outcome types with audited custom Debug boundaries; daemon snapshots use their redacted Debug and registry/install outcomes are already status-only or redacted. blocked_while_busy intentionally contains user-initiated state-changing/page-switch messages while allowing worker completions, owner/status reconciliation, progress ticks, modal dismissal, and other completion/control-plane events required to leave the busy state. The root still applies workflow-specific interceptors before this generic classification.

ASR provider management was reviewed end to end rather than only through its earlier view audit. Add mode defaults to Command and permits kind/id creation; edit mode preserves exact id/kind and hidden hotword fields. Local/Command/Remote construction clears irrelevant fields, parses positive optional timeout and JSON string-array arguments, rebuilds environment maps from visible keys plus SecretInput values, and keeps credential-bearing endpoints and process values out of Debug. Complete VinpstConfig validation runs before persistence, duplicate/stale provider snapshots fail closed, and custom removal refuses the active provider and registry-managed entries.

Provider mutation/removal workers use the shared conflict-aware validated atomic config save plus daemon reload boundary and refresh the ConfigDocument only after a successful result. Dirty Control, scene, LLM-provider and Hotword states block conflicting ASR provider operations. The final review also localized the ASR editor cross-operation guard while preserving its English wording exactly; the already-owned adapter editor, scene-editor guard, and dirty-Control resource guard received the same English/zh_CN treatment so all deterministic GUI-authored conflict copy follows GuiLocale.

Resource details remain a structural, secret-safe projection. Installed models expose typed display/runtime/family/language/size/file-count/path metadata but exclude raw recognizer/model/extra JSON; ASR providers expose kind/status/model/timeout, a redacted endpoint, hotword path, managed flag, and argument/environment counts without command/argument/environment contents; LLM providers expose model, redacted endpoint, credential-present and object/key counts; adapters expose managed/count/presence fields without command, args, env values, working directory, or extension values. Existing secret fixtures prove these exclusions and stale selections degrade to an unavailable modal rather than stale data.

Config persistence at the root revalidates on-disk equality, validates the complete edited config, uses the shared backup/0600/atomic writer, refuses reachable non-idle or active-session mutation, allows explicit offline saves when the daemon is unavailable, and on reload failure restores the previous document and requests a second daemon reload so disk and runtime do not silently diverge. headless_snapshot uses only config summary/count/public settings plus the already-sanitized runtime diagnostic JSON and the declared interaction capability snapshot.

Evidence includes complete source/call-site review of all four owned files; existing ASR provider add/edit/stale/removal/redaction/dirty-form tests; resource-detail secret fixtures and stale-selection tests; daemon snapshot and routing/busy/config rollback tests; the new App structural-Debug secret regression; localized guard template and ASR/adapter/control conflict tests; strict all-target vinpst-gui Clippy; full GUI suite and main test; docs build; secret scan; diff check; and module-parity ledger validation with zero remaining current or upstream pending files.

The repository-wide `just ci` source-layout gate exposed that the composition root had grown to 1,311 lines after its final diagnostic hardening, above the 1,200-line production limit. The redacted App Debug implementation and headless package-check projection were therefore extracted without behavioral changes into `app_diagnostics.rs`. The new file is owned by this same audit unit, keeping the ledger complete rather than creating new unowned current-only source; `lib.rs` remains the state/update composition root while diagnostic projection has a bounded owner.
